articles.title: Warrington 35-12 Hull KR: Matty Ashton hat-trick helps Wolves set up Super League semi-final vs Leeds as Peta Hiku sees red
articles.summary: Warrington Wolves set up a Super League semi-final with Leeds Rhinos after a 35-12 victory over reigning champions Hull KR in their eliminator showdown at the Halliwell Jones Stadium.
articles.body:
Warrington into semis for the first time since 2024; loss brings an end to Willie Peters' reign; Peta Hiku was shown a red card for punch on George Williams; the Super League semi-finals take place on Friday September 25 and Saturday September 26, live on Sky Sports

Warrington Wolves set up a Super League semi-final with Leeds Rhinos after a 35-12 victory over reigning champions Hull KR in their eliminator showdown at the Halliwell Jones Stadium.

It marks Warrington's first semi-final since 2024 after they missed out on the play-offs in 2025.

It also means Willie Peters' tenure as Robins head coach is now over after his reign which featured the history-making season in 2025 in which he won the Super League for the club for the first time.

The flashpoint of the game came early in the second half when Peta Hiku saw red for a punch on George Williams and the player advantage for Warrington eventually became too much for Hull KR to contend with.

Warrington had a narrow 12-6 lead at half-time thanks to a converted Ben Currie try, Ewan Irwin penalty and Matty Ashton's score. Hull KR hit back through a Joe Burgess wonder-try that was started by Arthur Mourgue to get themselves in the game.

After Hiku's red card, Ashton scored twice more to complete his hat-trick with Albert Hopoate also crossing the whitewash.

Hull KR had gone over through Dean Hadley but it ended up merely a consolation at the full-time whistle, Williams rubbing salt in the wound with a late drop goal and Toby King finishing things off with a try.

Warrington will head to play Leeds on Friday September 25, with kick-off at 8pm live on Sky Sports as they compete for a spot in the Grand Final. Wigan Warriors will then host Wakefield Trinity on Saturday September 26, with kick-off at 5.30pm on Sky Sports , as they bid to complete the final two.

Warrington a step closer to Grand Final as Peters era comes to close

After an early repeat set, it was not long until some eyes-up rugby saw Warrington get the first points on the board. Williams had some incredible vision to send the grubber kick through and while Burgess collected it, he half fumbled, which allowed Currie to collect and go in under the sticks.

Irwin converted and the home team were quickly 6-0 up, much to the delight of a packed-out Halliwell Jones Stadium.

Ill-discipline was costing the Robins and, once again, Warrington turned that into points. Irwin slotted over the penalty for offside and an eight-point lead was in place within 15 minutes.

Tries were then denied for both sides in corner-flying finishes from Ashton and Burgess that looked sublime, but neither winger could get the ball down before being bulldozed into touch.

With four minutes left of the half, the Robins scored a sensational full-length effort started off by a pass from Jack Broadbent to Mourgue who used his step and raced 70 metres before finding Burgess who did the rest. Mourgue converted and there were just two points in it.

That closeness did not last for long, as on the stroke of half-time, Kelepi Tanginoa broke through and found Ashton who used his pace to dive in for his 100th Super League try. Irwin's conversion attempt hit the post, so Warrington walked in with a 12-6 lead after 40 minutes of enthralling rugby league.

The key moment of the game came three minutes into the second half when a suspected punch from Hiku on Williams resulted in a red card. There was not much force in it but he hit the Warrington captain's face and left the Robins with 12 for the remainder.

Warrington made sure to immediately capitalise from it as they sent it out wide for Ashton to finish off his second try. It looked to be a forward pass but was given and so the Wolves were 16-6 up with 35 minutes remaining.

Despite being a player down, Hull KR would not give up and got their reward in the 53rd minute when a breakaway from Burgess was eventually finished by Hadley barrelling over from close range. Mourgue converted to bring the score to 16-12 and we had a game on our hands.

The tension had reached a new level inside Warrington's home but it was alleviated with just a quarter to go. James Bentley came up with a massive interception and Ashton followed to pick up from the play the ball and race away for his hat-trick.

That felt like the crucial score and Warrington then took control as Hopoate went in with a brilliant dive at the corner and Irwin came through clutch for a 16-point lead.

Just to rub salt in the wound, Williams sent over the one-pointer and, with a minute on the clock, King walked through and Irwin wrapped up the 35-12 victory and a spot in the semi-finals.

In the away end, there was extended applause for outgoing head coach Peters and the dynasty he has built. Burgess, meanwhile, celebrated on the pitch with his family as he continues his quest to do something just as monumental for Warrington.

Peters: Discipline cost us | Burgess: We should have closed out game earlier

Hull KR head coach Willie Peters, speaking to Sky Sports:

"Discipline has cost us a lot this year, and unfortunately it did again tonight, but I can't fault the players. I'm really proud of them. They kept fighting until the end.

"Warrington played really well and have been a very good team all year. I wish them all the best, but I'm really, really proud of this group and what they've achieved over the last four years. We've made a lot of beautiful memories.

"When you're down to 12 men it makes things difficult, but we still put ourselves in the game. We scored at the other end, went two points ahead and then, against the run of play, they scored.

"Fatigue always creeps in and it did towards the back end of the game. Peta has been great for us for three years. What he did was probably the wrong thing, but he's been outstanding for me throughout that time."

Warrington Wolves head coach Sam Burgess, speaking to Sky Sports:

"I'm proud of the group. It was a strange game, but we're pleased to come through and get another week together, which is what we came for. In the first half we felt really dominant and were disappointed with the scoreline.

"We left two or three tries out there and probably a couple more in the second half. We've just got to understand how important precision is because, over the course of a game, those moments add up. We could have finished the game much earlier."

Super League play-offs results and schedule

Friday September 18: Wakefield Trinity 26-16 Leigh Leopards

Saturday September 19: Warrington Wolves 35-12 Hull KR

Semi-Final 1 - Friday September 25: Leeds Rhinos vs Warrington Wolves, 8pm KO on Sky Sports

Semi-Final 2 - Saturday September 26: Wigan Warriors v Wakefield Trinity, 5.30pm KO on Sky Sports

The Super League play-offs are under way, live on Sky Sports, and continue all the way through until the Grand Final from Old Trafford on October 3.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Week 2 Fades & Busts: Top rookies likely belong on your bench
articles.summary: Fantasy football analyst Matt Okada highlights six players worth fading in Week 2.
articles.body:
Welcome to the second of 17 weekly articles spotlighting the fantasy fades of the week! I am your host, Matt Okada, and I'll be bringing you half a dozen potential busts each and every Friday, from now until fantasy championships.

As a note, just because a player earns a "fade" or "bust" designation doesn't automatically mean they should be benched — it depends on the rest of your roster or the options on your waiver wire. But you can expect them to fall short of expectations (when I get them right). I include a "What to Do" section for every player to help with that.

Without further ado, here is my list for Week 2 of the 2026 season.

Justin Herbert , QB, Chargers vs. Raiders

Losing Ladd McConkey last week was devastating for the Chargers offense. Check out these numbers, courtesy of Next Gen Stats: with McConkey on the field, they averaged 6.3 yards per play, and on 17 dropbacks, Herbert logged a 128.4 passer rating, 10.3 yards per attempt and a 47.1% first-down rate. With McConkey off the field , L.A. averaged 4.2 yards per play, and on 17 dropbacks, Herbert dropped to a 42.3 passer rating, 5.4 yards per attempt and an 11.8% first-down rate.

McConkey was their best receiver by far and the engine of the offense ... but suffered a rib injury in the second half and is currently day-to-day (and not practicing).

In what feels like the unlikely chance McConkey plays on Sunday, it will likely be in a somewhat limited fashion. That's not encouraging for Herbert's fantasy prospects. Also, the Raiders significantly improved their defense on paper this offseason, and it showed — albeit, against the Dolphins — in Week 1. Nakobe Dean , Kwity Paye , Quay Walker and Treydan Stukes all made impact plays ... and centerpiece Maxx Crosby had 1.5 sacks of his own. Herbert is incredibly talented, but there are red flags heading into Week 2.

What to do ❓ Herbert is outside my top-12 quarterbacks for the week, so if you have a capable QB2 or a streamer, play them instead. That certainly includes guys like Brock Purdy , Jaxson Dart and Trevor Lawrence , but it also might include Jordan Love , Baker Mayfield or even Bryce Young .

Quinshon Judkins , RB, Browns vs. Buccaneers

Sometimes in fantasy, a running back can be useful despite playing for a subpar offense. For that to occur, they usually need to be an excellent receiver or have an excellent offensive line (or ideally both). Unfortunately, Quinshon Judkins has neither ... and his offense isn't just subpar, it's atrocious. In Week 1, Cleveland only cracked the red zone twice, and only scored one field goal on those two drives (the other, they turned the ball over on downs). Only one of their first six drives ended in Jacksonville territory (and it concluded with a Deshaun Watson interception).

Meanwhile, Judkins totaled just 33 rushing yards (fewer than Watson) on 12 carries, and his 2.8 yards per carry, 25% success rate, -0.25 EPA/carry and zero explosive runs were all bottom-tier among running backs. He caught two passes for 17 yards, which was a very slight improvement over his averages from 2025, but simply not enough in a game Cleveland trailed from start to finish. Until something changes drastically for the Browns — if it ever does — Judkins is going to be very hard to trust on a weekly basis. In a game where the Browns are 8.5-point underdogs against the Buccaneers, with an implied total of 16.5 points, he's well outside RB2 territory.

What to do ❓ If you don't have a better option, Judkins will likely see double-digit touches, which makes him an "okay" play in your FLEX. But he is not an RB2, and in any form of PPR scoring, it's probably smarter to look to a mid-range wide receiver like Stefon Diggs or Jalen Coker .

Jeremiyah Love, RB, Cardinals vs. Seahawks

It's going to be tough to bench Jeremiyah Love, considering how talented he is and what his draft capital insinuates for his (eventual) usage. But we have to work with the data we have. In Week 1, coming off a preseason ankle sprain, Love logged fewer snaps, carries and rushing yards than Tyler Allgeier , who's still technically listed as the starter on their depth chart. Additionally, Love saw just 2.8 expected yards per carry, fewest among all running backs with at least five carries in Week 1, and averaged -0.7 yards before contact per carry, ahead of only the Pittsburgh backs and the Atlanta backs.

While Love did his best to make the most out of the hand he was dealt — forcing six missed tackles and gaining 4.5 yards after contact per carry — it's going to be hard for the rookie to post consistent RB1 numbers in this offense. Now, he draws a matchup with the Seahawks in Week 2. They've allowed the lowest explosive run rate and EPA/carry to running backs since the start of last season and are second against the position in success rate, yards before contact per carry and missed tackle rate on rushes. Long story short, they're probably the toughest matchup for RBs and Love is already starting at a disadvantage in this offense.

What to do ❓ Love is still a borderline starter based on usage and talent, but there's a real chance he's a full dud against this defense. If you can pivot to someone like David Montgomery , D'Andre Swift, Rhamondre Stevenson or Chuba Hubbard , do it. And as with Judkins, look to a wide receiver in your FLEX instead, if possible.

On the one hand, DK Metcalf racked up 10 targets in Week 1 against the Falcons, more than triple what Michael Pittman Jr. saw (three) and four more than the next-closest Steelers wideout ( Roman Wilson , six). On the other hand, he caught just four of those targets for 40 yards, fewer catches than Pat Freiermuth and Jaylen Warren , and fewer yards than Pittman (58). Metcalf was officially credited with one drop, but looked off and out of sync with Aaron Rodgers for most of the game.

But this fade has less to do with Metcalf, Rodgers and their apparent lack of chemistry, and more to do with Christian Gonzalez . The Patriots cornerback tends to shadow No. 1 receivers, as he did against Metcalf the last time they met, back in 2024. In that game, Metcalf caught four of seven targets for just 27 yards when matched up with Gonzalez, which was 82% of his routes. Last week, Jaxon Smith-Njigba saw Gonzalez on 64% of his routes and did not catch either of his two targets in that matchup. You're getting a nightmare matchup for a receiver who's already on the fringe of fantasy lineups.

What to do ❓ Bench DK Metcalf. There are a number of FLEX-level wide receivers worth playing over him ... and I'd prefer teammate Michael Pittman Jr. in the same game.

Carnell Tate is an eerily fitting "wide receiver version" of the Jeremiyah Love fade this week. He was literally drafted the pick after Love back in April, and is incredibly talented, but plays in one of the most ineffective offenses in the league and has a terrible matchup this Sunday.

Let's start with the offense. Tennessee made it to the red zone just once in Week 1 — the only team worse on that count was the Falcons (zero) — with 2:42 remaining in the game (and the touchdown went to Elic Ayomanor ). Meanwhile, Cam Ward completed just 59.4% of his passes for 4.4 yards per attempt (dead last in Week 1), while averaging just 5.7 air yards per attempt (sixth-lowest). While Tate did see six targets in the game, all of that context is detrimental to his game and his fantasy upside.

Now, he takes on the Eagles and their outside cornerbacks, Quinyon Mitchell and Riq Woolen . Philly surrendered just 5.9 fantasy points to Washington's outside receivers in Week 1 (fewest in the league), while allowing Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams to thrive out of the slot. I'm not particularly excited about Wan'Dale Robinson in Tennessee's offense either, but this matchup favors him over Tate significantly.

What to do ❓ As with Metcalf, it's straight to the bench with Tate. It doesn't matter where you drafted him, there are at least 40 wide receivers worth playing this week instead. Not to mention, a rash of running backs who would be better suited in your FLEX.

Kyle Pitts Sr., TE, Falcons vs. Panthers

At this point, you might have noticed a theme to this week's column: we are avoiding the offenses that looked truly abysmal in Week 1. And, unfortunately, Atlanta's probably takes the cake in that respect. Third-string QB Cooper Rush logged the lowest passer rating (51.9), completion rate over expected (-21.3%) and success rate (30.8%) in Week 1, connecting on just 12 of 22 passes. And to make matters worse, none of those 12 connections went to Kyle Pitts Sr., who posted a fantasy bagel on just one target. Rush is likely to start again in Week 2, but I'm honestly not comfortable starting Pitts even if/when Tua Tagovailoa or Michael Penix Jr . returns to health, until we see this offense function at a reasonable level.

To make matters worse, Carolina has a long and storied history of turning Pitts into a fantasy bust. In 10 games against his division rival, the tight end has only topped nine fantasy points once , all the way back in Week 8, 2022. On the whole, he's averaged 6.1 fantasy points per game in this matchup, with fewer than six points in five of their last six meetings. There are essentially no green flags, and plenty of red ones, for Pitts heading into Week 2.

What to do ❓ I know the position is shallow, but try to find a tight end to stream over Pitts this week. That list absolutely includes Isaiah Likely , who is now a strong TE1, but also includes names like Juwan Johnson , Michael Mayer , Dalton Schultz and Jake Ferguson .

articles.title: Probamos los nuevos Dongfeng Vigo y Mage: dos SUV chinos con etiqueta Cero desde 26.615 euros
articles.standfirst: El Vigo eléctrico apuesta por el espacio y las soluciones prácticas; el Mage combina 299 CV con hasta 89 km eléctricos. Los hemos conducido y hay detalles que sorprenden, aunque también conviene examinar sus precios
articles.summary: El Vigo eléctrico apuesta por el espacio y las soluciones prácticas; el Mage combina 299 CV con hasta 89 km eléctricos. Los hemos conducido y hay detalles que sorprenden, aunque también conviene examinar sus precios
articles.body: Hace apenas dos años Dongfeng desembarcaba oficialmente en España con una gama que podía resumirse bastante rápido: el pequeño Box eléctrico. Ahora la firma china acaba de presentar el Vigo, un SUV urbano cien por cien eléctrico, y el Mage PHEV, su primer híbrido enchufable en nuestro mercado. Dos coches, dos tamaños y dos planteamientos distintos, pero una estrategia común: mucho equipamiento, precios ajustados y una garantía difícil de ignorar (aunque hay que leer bien la letra pequeña), de siete años o 300.000 kilómetros para el vehículo y diez años sin límite de kilometraje para la batería y el sistema eléctrico de propulsión. Dongfeng cuenta ya con 25 concesionarios en España y pretende cerrar 2026 con 30 y alcanzar los 45 en 2027. El Vigo ocupa el escalón intermedio de la gama Dongfeng con sus 4,3 metros de longitud y me parece una propuesta especialmente pensada para un uso urbano y familiar. Su diseño es bastante discreto, sin buscar llamar la atención a toda costa, aunque recupera alguna solución que personalmente me ha encantado. La más evidente está en el maletero. El portón cuenta con apertura partida, con una sección inferior independiente que facilita mucho el acceso a la zona de carga. Me parece especialmente práctico para meter maletas, subir a una mascota o cargar material deportivo sin tener que levantarlo todo desde el suelo. Es uno de esos detalles sencillos que, cuando lo utilizas, entiendes rápidamente su utilidad. Además la parte de abajo soporta hasta 150 kg y se puede utilizar como mesa improvisada. Por concepto, espacio y soluciones prácticas, veo al Vigo como un coche pensado para alguien con espíritu joven, que busca un vehículo fácil para el día a día pero necesita cierta versatilidad para escapadas, deporte o viajes. Al volante, una de las cosas que más me sorprendió fue su ángulo de giro. En ciudad se nota enseguida, porque permite maniobrar con mucha facilidad y resolver giros en calles estrechas sin necesidad de hacer varias correcciones. Es un detalle que puede parecer menor en una ficha técnica, pero que en el uso diario marca diferencias, sobre todo en aparcamientos, garajes y zonas urbanas donde cada centímetro cuenta. También me llamó la atención el espacio interior, especialmente en las plazas traseras. Hay mucho sitio para las piernas y bastante altura libre al techo. Incluso una persona de alrededor de 1,90 metros puede viajar detrás con comodidad, algo que no siempre ocurre en un SUV de este tamaño. El Mage juega claramente en otra categoría. Es un coche más grande y esa sensación aparece desde el momento en que me siento al volante. Porque la posición de conducción ofrece muy buena visibilidad, algo que agradecí especialmente teniendo en cuenta sus dimensiones. Desde el asiento del conductor controlo bien lo que ocurre alrededor del coche. Todo resulta intuitivo y fácil de manejar. El nivel de equipamiento también es uno de sus puntos fuertes. Durante la prueba me gustaron especialmente los asientos calefactados y ventilados, además del volante calefactado, elementos que quizá no parezcan imprescindibles hasta que empiezas a utilizarlos. El equipamiento llega prácticamente cerrado e incluye elementos como el techo panorámico, el portón eléctrico, cámaras de visión periférica y numerosos asistentes de conducción. Otra cosa que me ha gustado es la memoria de posición del asiento del conductor. Su funcionamiento resulta realmente sencillo e intuitivo, algo que agradezco en un coche cargado de tecnología, porque encontrar una función no siempre significa poder utilizarla con rapidez. Muchas de las funciones del vehículo se controlan desde la gran pantalla central. Personalmente sigo prefiriendo disponer de algunos mandos físicos para las operaciones más habituales, pero reconozco que el sistema del Mage permite concentrar prácticamente toda la gestión del coche en un mismo lugar. Y hay un detalle especialmente importante para nuestro mercado: el techo panorámico practicable incorpora cortinilla. Puede parecer algo evidente, pero con el sol y las temperaturas que tenemos durante buena parte del año en España, se agradece —y mucho— poder cerrarla. El Dongfeng Mage cambia completamente el planteamiento respecto al Vigo.Con 4,69 metros de longitud juega en una categoría superior y también sube varios escalones en prestaciones respecto al Vigo. Su sistema híbrido enchufable combina un motor 1.5 turbo de gasolina con otro eléctrico para alcanzar 299 CV de potencia conjunta. La batería tiene 17 kWh y Dongfeng anuncia hasta 89 kilómetros de autonomía eléctrica y hasta 1.200 kilómetros combinando gasolina y electricidad. Eso sí, hay que apuntar que esos números (89 y 1.200 kilómetros) que nos ofreció el fabricante corresponden al ciclo de homologación chino, por lo que no deben compararse directamente con una homologación europea WLTP, más exigente y, por tanto, menos optimista. Dongfeng declara además 4,8 l/100 km con la batería descargada, un dato quizá más útil para quien realmente vaya a utilizar el coche en viajes largos que el habitual consumo homologado de un PHEV con la batería llena (que en este caso es de 1,5 l/100). El Mage permite además carga rápida en corriente continua a 22 kW, algo todavía poco habitual entre los híbridos enchufables, y puede recuperar del 30 al 80% de la batería en unos 31 minutos (este dato es diferente al ) El precio de tarifa anunciado inicialmente es de 29.990 euros para el Vigo y 31.990 euros para el Mage PHEV, antes de determinadas promociones o ayudas. Durante la presentación, Dongfeng comunicó precios promocionales desde 26.615 euros para el Vigo y 28.740 euros para el Mage, sujetos a campañas y condiciones comerciales. El Box permitió a Dongfeng poner un pie en España. El Vigo y el Mage son los coches con los que intenta empezar a hacerse un sitio de verdad. El Vigo tiene argumentos claros como eléctrico urbano y familiar: espacio, carga rápida y mucho equipamiento. El Mage juega la baza de la versatilidad, con casi 300 CV, autonomía eléctrica suficiente para muchos desplazamientos diarios y un motor de gasolina que elimina la preocupación por los viajes largos.

"Fatigue always creeps in and it did towards the back end of the game. Peta has been great for us for three years. What he did was probably the wrong thing, but he's been outstanding for me throughout that time."

Warrington Wolves head coach Sam Burgess, speaking to Sky Sports:

"I'm proud of the group. It was a strange game, but we're pleased to come through and get another week together, which is what we came for. In the first half we felt really dominant and were disappointed with the scoreline.

"We left two or three tries out there and probably a couple more in the second half. We've just got to understand how important precision is because, over the course of a game, those moments add up. We could have finished the game much earlier."

articles.title: James Rodríguez revive su paso por la Selección Colombia y su comienzo con Nacional: "Me dieron mucho"
articles.standfirst: El 10 entregó las primeras palabras sobre el fútbol colombiano y de lo su ciclo en la Selección Colombia
articles.summary: El 10 entregó las primeras palabras sobre el fútbol colombiano y de lo su ciclo en la Selección Colombia
articles.body: Aun estando al margen de las convocatorias de la Selección Colombia tras anunciar su retiro definitivo de la 'Tricolor', el nombre de James Rodríguez sigue retumbando en la memoria y el corazón de los aficionados. En sus primeras declaraciones oficiales refiriéndose a su ciclo con el combinado nacional en tiempo pasado, el cucuteño volvió a conmover al país al reflexionar sobre sus casi 16 años vistiendo la camiseta '10'. Las emotivas palabras del mediocampista se dieron en una entrevista concedida a los canales oficiales de Atlético Nacional, club al que llegó recientemente y con el cual debutó con victoria por 3-2 sobre Internacional de Bogotá en la Liga BetPlay. Reflexionando sobre su largo recorrido con la camiseta tricolor, que incluyó actuaciones históricas como la Bota de Oro en el Mundial de Brasil 2014, el volante dejó en claro el sentido de gratitud que siente hacia la hinchada colombiana. “Yo lo único que intenté fue hacer feliz a todo un país, darlo todo por esa camiseta, fueron 15 años, casi 16. Intentaba hacer el trabajo mío, ganar, y eso va de la mano para hacer feliz a todo un país”, expresó James durante la entrevista. Además, envió un cálido mensaje al público que lo respaldó durante más de una década en las eliminatorias y torneos internacionales: “Los hinchas no me deben nada, al contrario, agradecerles a ellos por todo el cariño que me dan, por todo el cariño que me han mostrado estas últimas horas”, añadió. A sus 35 años y tras una extensa trayectoria en el fútbol europeo y continental desde su salida de Banfield en 2007, James enfoca ahora todo su talento en el fútbol profesional colombiano vistiendo los colores de Atlético Nacional. En su debut oficial con el 'Verdolaga' en Bogotá, el cucuteño ingresó desde el banquillo para marcar la diferencia en la parte complementaria, asistiendo con un centro preciso a Zapata para sellar la victoria del equipo antioqueño. Sobre el recibimiento por parte de los aficionados en el Nemesio Camacho El Campín y su llegada al equipo más ganador del país, James destacó: “Estoy feliz, son muchos años fuera, desde el 2007, y ver todo ese cariño fue algo único. Eso quiere decir que he hecho las cosas bien durante muchos años (...). Impone todo lo que ha ganado este club, todos los títulos, es un club histórico. Espero hacer historia aquí también”. Más allá del brillo con el balón, la recta final del partido estuvo marcada por la alta temperatura sobre el césped. James sintió el rigor del fútbol colombiano al recibir varias entradas fuertes por parte de la zona defensiva y medular del conjunto rival, destacando un cruce verbal con los futbolistas Johan Caballero y Larry Vásquez tras una dura infracción en los minutos finales. "Siempre, siempre, pero yo creo que aquí van a dar más. Pero bueno, aquí los árbitros son buenos y van a ayudar a proteger a los que juegan bien. Me dieron mucho… Salí de casa bien, me voy, y llego y mira, ¿qué me van a decir, que en dónde estaba? Pero eso hace parte del fútbol, hace parte de todo. Son heridas de guerra", concluye.

articles.title: At 17, New York student Liam Anderson breaks national bench press record with 396 pounds, then breaks his own record again with 402 pounds
articles.summary: International Sports News: Liam Anderson went into the 2026 USA Powerlifting Southwest Regional Championships with one clear goal: break the national bench press record in his a.
articles.body: Liam Anderson went into the 2026 USA Powerlifting Southwest Regional Championships with one clear goal: break the national bench press record in his age and weight class before turning 18 later this month. The Shenendehowa High School senior did more than that. During the September 5 competition in Grapevine, Texas, Anderson first lifted 180 kilograms, or about 396 pounds, on his second attempt to set a new American record. He then returned for his final attempt, lifted 182.5 kilograms, or about 402 pounds, and broke the record he had just set only moments earlier.How did Liam Anderson break the national record twice?Anderson competed in the 16-to-17 age division and the up-to-82.5-kilogram weight class, which is around 182 pounds. He entered the competition knowing that this could be one of his final chances to set the record before moving into a new age group after turning 18.The teenager had spent the month before the competition preparing specifically for the record attempt. His training was built around getting his body and mind ready to handle the weight he knew he would need to lift in Texas.His second attempt was the first big moment of the day. Anderson successfully pressed 180 kilograms, or around 396 pounds. The lift was enough to break the existing American record for the 16-to-17 age group at up to 82.5 kilograms.But Anderson was not finished. He still had one attempt remaining, and instead of simply protecting the record he had already earned, he decided to raise the weight. He put 182.5 kilograms on the bar, which is roughly 402 pounds, and went back for his final lift.Anderson completed the attempt. That meant he had broken the national record twice in the same competition. His first successful lift created a new record, and his final lift pushed the mark even higher.Anderson later told NEWS10 ABC that he felt very confident before his second attempt because he had trained specifically for the record during the month leading up to the competition. The third attempt, however, felt different. He said he did not know what would happen when he stepped up to the bar and described the final lift as being driven by pure adrenaline.Anderson also said he was thinking about his mother during that final attempt. When the lift was completed, 182.5 kilograms became his new national record.How did Liam Anderson become a record-setting powerlifter so quickly?Anderson’s rise is especially interesting because he has not been competing in powerlifting for a very long time. He only started lifting in 2025, meaning much of his progress has come in a relatively short period.His competitive career with USA Powerlifting became more active in early 2026. He quickly began making a name for himself in his age and weight class, and his performances showed that he could compete with some of the strongest young lifters in the country.Before his record-breaking performance in Texas, Anderson had already set a New York State record in his age and weight class in November 2025. That achievement gave him another target to chase.As his strength continued to improve, Anderson began focusing on the national record. The timing made the goal even more important because his 18th birthday was approaching later in September.Once Anderson turned 18, he would leave the 16-to-17 age division and move into a new age group. That left him with a limited amount of time to make his attempt. The Southwest Regional Championships came at the right moment.Anderson had spent the month before the competition training with the national record in mind. Rather than simply hoping for a good performance, he had a specific number he wanted to reach.In the end, he reached it and then went beyond it. His two successful lifts turned what could have been a normal competition into the biggest moment of his young powerlifting career.What happened when Anderson competed at Bench Nationals?The record in Texas came after another important competition for Anderson earlier in 2026.In July, he competed at Bench Nationals. Although he did not break the American record at that event, his performance still brought him an important achievement.Anderson earned a place on the USA Powerlifting National Bench Press Team.The result showed that his progress was not limited to one competition. By that point, he had already established himself as a serious young competitor in the sport.Anderson was also invited to represent the United States at the 2026 International Drug Free Powerlifting Association World Championships in Hjalteyri, Iceland, in October.However, he decided not to compete at the world championships because the trip would conflict with his school schedule.That decision did not change his focus.Instead, Anderson continued training and kept working toward the national record he wanted to break before his 18th birthday. The work eventually paid off at the Southwest Regional Championships.His performance there also gave him a memorable way to finish his time in the 16-to-17 division. Rather than leaving the age group with one national record, he left it after setting the mark twice during the same competition.What is next for Liam Anderson after breaking the record?Anderson already has another goal waiting for him. After setting the 182.5-kilogram national record, he said he wants to chase the world record in the 18-to-19 age division once he moves up. He also has a long-term goal of bench pressing 500 pounds before turning 20.For a teenager who only began lifting in 2025, his progress has happened quickly. In less than two years, he has gone from starting out in the gym to setting a New York State record, competing at Bench Nationals, earning a place on the USA Powerlifting National Bench Press Team and breaking the national bench press record twice in one competition.It is also important to understand the sport behind Anderson’s achievement. Powerlifting is different from Olympic weightlifting. Powerlifting includes the squat, bench press and deadlift, while weightlifting is based on the snatch and the clean and jerk. Some powerlifting competitions focus on all three lifts, while others, such as bench press competitions, focus on a specific lift.USA Powerlifting is a drug-tested powerlifting organization in the United States. It was established in 1981 as the American Drug Free Powerlifting Association.Anderson now moves into a new stage of his career. His 16-to-17 age division ends with a 182.5-kilogram, or about 402-pound, national record beside his name. His next challenge will be competing in the 18-to-19 division and seeing how far he can take the strength he has built in such a short time.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Willie Peters era at Hull KR ends after eliminator loss: 'Thank you for the memories, I will miss you dearly'
articles.summary: Hull KR will not defend their Betfred Super League title at Old Trafford after losing to Warrington in the eliminators; It brings an end to Willie Peters' four-year reign at the Robins in which he helped them to a historic treble
articles.body:
That was thanks to the guidance of Willie Peters. In his third year in charge of the club, he helped them 'climb Everest' and make history.

Not only did they win the Betfred Super League, they picked up the League Leaders' Shield and Challenge Cup, and then topped that off with a World Club Challenge win over Brisbane Broncos.

Every trophy was theirs. They simply were the team to beat, but no one could.

It was announced part way through this season that 2026 would mark Peters' final season in charge of the Robins before he heads to pastures new to take charge of the NRL's newest franchise, the PNG Chiefs.

The task was set: Finish on a high for their leader. Unfortunately for those from east Hull, they did not get the fairytale ending to close out Peters' four years in charge as they went out in the eliminators to Warrington Wolves after finishing sixth in the table.

However, Peters views it as "the best four years of his life" of which he is immensely proud.

"Discipline has cost us a lot this year, and unfortunately tonight, but I can't fault them," Peters told Sky Sports after the defeat at Warrington.

"I am really proud of them. They kept fighting to the end. Warrington played really well and have been a very good team all year. I wish them all the best, but I'm really, really proud of the group and proud of what they've achieved over the last four years at the club. We've made a lot of beautiful memories.

"When you're down to 12 men it makes it difficult, but we put ourselves in the game. We scored down the other end, went two points ahead and then, against the run of play, they scored.

"Fatigue always creeps in and it did towards the back end of the game. Peta (Hiku) has been great for us for three years. What he did [get sent off] was probably the wrong thing, but he's been outstanding for me over the last three years.

"We've got a lot of great memories, that's for sure, but they're still here, still cheering for their team. We're a close-knit club. We're a club that wanted to win trophies, and we have, but the fight tonight shows what this place is about.

"We were well beaten, but we still showed a lot of fight. My family and I have had an absolute ball. We've loved it over here and we'll never forget our time at Hull KR.

"I do feel loved, absolutely. Love's important. I remember Russell Crowe saying years ago at South (Sydney Rabbitohs) that it's all about the love, and there's something in that.

"When you're part of a family and create the right environment, especially in sport, where everyone cares about each other, you can do wonderful things.

"There's no doubt I've felt the love from the fans and the players, and vice versa. I love them too. When there's genuine care and love for each other, you can achieve special things.

"I love it over here. I'm really looking forward to the next chapter and to having a positive impact on a country (Papua New Guinea) through rugby league, both on and off the field.

"It's similar to what we've done here, but on a bigger scale. I'm really excited about that challenge."

Peters to return to Super League one day? 'Never say never'

While this particular chapter is closed for Peters and he has ticked off his goal of coaching in Super League, he admits he will never close the book on the UK.

But for now, he is focused on achieving the next goal which is being a head coach in the NRL.

Despite that, he will continue to back the European competition and ensure it gets the "recognition it deserves".

"We have loved it here. This has been home, and probably this year was the first time it really felt like home, which made it even harder knowing I was leaving. My family and I have loved it, so you never say never," he added.

"I am proud. I've got a great support network and I've loved working with everyone. You've all been great. The rugby league community over here has been fantastic. The game is in a positive place and I think there's a lot of growth ahead in the next few years.

"The product is outstanding and it's finally getting the recognition it deserves, even in Australia.

"I don't think Super League has always received the respect it merits, but I've always respected it. That's why I played here and why I always wanted to coach here.

"I'm proud to have been involved in Super League as a coach, and now I've got some goals to tick off when I return to the NRL.

"Just thank you for the memories and thank you for the support they've given me. They've made me a better person and a better coach.

"I've now got an opportunity to return to the NRL, something I've always wanted to do, and it's purely because of what they've achieved.

"At the end of the day, the players decide how hard they want to work and where they want to get to, and they've been massive for me and my family.

"I also want to acknowledge the board, who have been incredibly supportive. Everyone at Hull KR, I'm going to miss dearly. Thank you to everyone, including the away fans. The support I've received has been incredible. So, thank you."

articles.title: ‘He’s a workaholic’ – Dirk Nowitzki gives his analysis on Cooper Flagg’s rookie season and future potential
articles.summary: Dallas Mavericks legend Dirk Nowitzki has shared what he felt about Cooper Flagg’s rookie season, and what the future has in store for the 2025 number one ov...
articles.body:
Dallas Mavericks legend Dirk Nowitzki has shared what he felt about Cooper Flagg 's rookie season, and what the future has in store for the 2025 number one overall pick.

Last year, Flagg was drafted after the franchise had lost its superstar Luka Doncic due to a decision made by Nico Harrison, who was fired from his role following a poor start to the 2025-26 season by the Mavs.

There was a lot of hype around him, as he had been a solid player throughout high school and college. He certainly lived up to it, averaging 21 points per game and 6.7 rebounds as a rookie.

With the team not playing well, Flagg was the only bright light for the Mavs.

Dirk Nowitzki, who serves as a special advisor for the Mavs, revealed the conversations he had with the rookie during his first year.

With the departure of Doncic, the reins of the team are now with Flagg, and he has shown the talent to carry the franchise for the coming years.

Nowitzki, who did the same for two decades, spoke about the player, and what made him special.

"He's had a terrific first season," Nowitzki told reporters at his foundation event, according to Abby Jones of DLLS Sports . "The hype that he had as a No. 1 pick, to basically live through that and exceed that hype, has been incredible to watch in Year 1.

"How he got better from week-to-week, from month-to-month. We all know he's a workaholic, loves hoops. That's all he does. He wants to get better, he wants to add things to his repertoire. So, I think he's gonna have a great second season and sky is the limit for him. Hopefully, we can watch him for the next decade plus."

Initially, the Mavs had Flagg play primarily as a point guard, something Jason Kidd was trying out which resulted in them having a poor start to the season.

As the season progressed, though, Flagg's confidence grew, and he delivered some big performances. The rookie also reached out to Nowitzki and asked for advice.

"I'll write him a few things when I see something," Nowitzki said.

"He knows that I'm in his corner. I want him to succeed and do well, but like I said, he's so far ahead of the curve already at that age. But if there's ever anything that he needs, I'm more than happy to help."

Nico Collins is facing an extended absence after suffering a hamstring injury during the Houston Texans ' practice this week. The wide receiver has already been ruled out for Sunday's matchup with the Cincinnati Bengals , leaving Houston without one of its most important offensive players.

Collins entered the 2026 NFL season as a major part of the Texans' passing game after establishing himself as C.J. Stroud 's top receiving option. He opened the season with a strong performance against the Buffalo Bills , showing his importance to the offense from the start.

The injury now creates a significant issue for Houston as it prepares for its second game of the season. The latest update also raises the possibility that Collins could miss more than just Sunday's matchup.

Collins did not participate in Houston's Thursday or Friday sessions.

The injury is a Grade 1 hamstring strain, according to Aaron Wilson. Collins will not be placed on injured reserve at this point, but the Texans could be without him beyond Week 2 as he works back from the injury.

Collins had already made an impact in Week 1. He caught seven of 10 targets for 75 yards and a touchdown against the Bills. He also added seven rushing yards on one carry.

articles.title: 5 takeaways from Penn State’s rout over Buffalo
articles.summary: Penn State dominated the Buffalo Bulls today, so let’s look at five major takeaways from the blowout win.
articles.body:
Now that looked more like Penn State football. Head coach Matt Campbell was clearly unsatisfied with his team's performance last week in a sloppy game against Temple , and he took it out on Buffalo today.

The Nittany Lions had all three phases working again in Week 3, with 55 points from the offense, another masterful performance from the defense, and a couple of special punt returns by wide receiver Zay Robinson . The team looked like a well-oiled machine as they wrapped up their final game before they start competing against Big Ten opponents next week.

Of course, there are always things to clean up, but today was much prettier than last Saturday. Let's look at five things that were key to giving Penn State a win today.

We have highlighted defensive coordinator D'Anton Lynn before, so the fact that he's still impressing shows just how dominant his defense has been. He does such a good job of mixing up the pressure packages, often sending linebackers on blitzes and then fooling the defense when they switch it up and drop back into coverage.

The open-field tackling has been one of the glaring strengths so far this season, with a swarm of Nittany Lions defenders around the ball as soon as it is caught or handed off. Lynn's impact has been evident, as the defense has yet to surrender more than one touchdown in a game this season. Now, it's time to see if his unit plays at the same level when conference play begins.

Offensive coordinator Taylor Mouser finally got the ground game going today. Penn State flashed potential in that area in the first two weeks, but the strong runs were few and far between.

This week, running backs James Peoples and Quinton Marin Jr. finally made some explosive runs, with the latter having the highlight of the day, which was a 61-yard burst up the sideline. Martin Jr. nearly scored on the run but tripped over his own feet before he made it to the end zone.

The run blocking was great, each rusher that got carries made an impact, and the young men in the backfield just jumped off the screen all day. It won't be as easy to throw up and down the field against Big Ten teams, so the emergence of the run game is a welcome sight.

The Nittany Lions have been solid on special teams to begin the year — they just lacked the splash plays to prove it. Robinson changed that this week with two punt returns that went for more than 30 yards. He almost added a third to his total, but it was called back due to a questionable block in the back call.

Nonetheless, he set his team up with excellent field position all afternoon and managed to be one of the most impactful players without touching the ball much on offense. It will make Penn State much tougher to defend if it gets the ball in the opponent's territory as often as today.

Robinson did get banged up in the second half, but returned to the game shortly after. Hopefully it wasn't just adrenaline allowing him to push through and he's truly healthy.

Defensive end Max Granville was tragically lost to another season-ending injury before last week's win over the Owls. That meant that some of the other pass rushers, like Yvan Kemajou and Alexander McPherson , needed to step up.

That's exactly what they did, sacking Bulls quarterback Jason Wright once and getting in his face a bunch more. Penn State's defensive line was in the backfield all day long and it made it difficult for Wright to have any success throwing the ball. He threw for only 60 yards thanks to the relentless pass rush of the Blue and White and the sticky coverage from the secondary.

Wide receiver Koby Howard looked like a star in Week 1, but we needed to see more to make sure it was real. If you weren't sure before, you should be now, because Howard showed everything you'd want to see out of a receiver against Buffalo .

His first catch of the game was a phenomenal leaping grab over a defender in the first quarter on an underthrown ball by quarterback Rocco Becht . In the second quarter, Mouser got creative and got the ball to Howard on a double reverse that he took 20 yards for a touchdown.

Then, he had a 70-yard catch-and-run touchdown later in the quarter to put his team up 31 points. Howard continues to dazzle audiences and put new ceilings on just how successful this passing game can become this season.

articles.title: Key Auburn stats to consider as Florida heads into SEC play
articles.summary: Florida is preparing to enter a hostile environment at Jordan-Hare Stadium in Week 3. Here is what Gators fans need to know as kickoff approaches.
articles.body:
Florida 's first SEC opponent will present a different challenge than the Gators faced in the opening two weeks.

Auburn enters Saturday night winners of their first pair of games as well. First-year head coach Alex Golesh led the Tigers to victories over Baylor and Southern Mississippi; Auburn averaged 501 yards of total offense per game to start the season — that ranks No. 8 in the SEC.

Auburn's rushing game has been especially potent to begin the 2026 campaign with consecutive 300-yard performances for the first time since 2021. Quarterback Byrum Brown is the main catalyst of that attack — against Southern Mississippi, the senior accounted for 319 total yards and three touchdowns. He also completed 18 of 29 passes for 226 yards while adding an additional 88 on the ground.

Brown is flanked by Omar Mabson III, who rushed for 108 yards against Southern Mississippi, and Jeremiah Cobb , who added 85. Overall, the Tigers had three players eclipse 80 yards rushing in the 43-8 win.

One thing to watch in Saturday's game is how well the Tigers do on third down. Thus far, Golesh's team is 17 of 33 when attempting to extend drives. Four of those five conversions have come in the fourth quarter. Florida 's defense is allowing opponents to convert 40% of the time in the same scenario.

Defensively, Auburn has yet to surrender a rushing touchdown this season. That creates quite an intriguing matchup against star running back Jadan Baugh and a Florida rushing attack that averages 247.5 yards per game.

One final statistic to highlight is kicker Alex McPherson 's 94 career extra points, on which he is perfect throughout his career. If Saturday's game is close, McPherson has already connected on a 55-yard field goal against Southern Mississippi.

articles.title: McConnell, Moorehouse & O'Rourke through to medal bouts
articles.summary: Jon McConnell, Daina Moorehouse and Lisa O'Rourke are all through to medal fights in the European Boxing Championships, but Shannon Sweeney misses out on a q...
articles.body:
Jon McConnell, Daina Moorehouse and Lisa O'Rourke are all through to medal fights in the European Boxing Championships, but Shannon Sweeney missed out on a quarter-final place after defeat in Sofia on Saturday.

Commonwealth Games gold medallist McConnell, who beat Turkey's Necat Ekinci on Thursday, claimed a 4-1 unanimous decision win against Poland's Damian Durkacz in his last-16 bout.

The 23-year-old will now face Italy's Gabriele Guidi Rontani in the quarter-finals on Monday.

Moorehouse also progressed to the last eight as she beat Bulgarian home favourite Zlatislava Chukanova, who she also overcame in the Olympic qualifiers for Paris, by split decision.

The 25-year-old Wicklow fighter was forced to take a count in the final round but still claimed the 3-2 win and will now take on World and European bronze medallist Laura Fuentes Fernandez from Spain in the next round.

O'Rourke, the 2022 World champion, marked her return to the ring with a unanimous decision win over Greece's Vasiliki Stavridou in her last-16 fight.

After dominating the first two rounds, she then forced two standing counts in the last to ease to victory and will come up against Team GB's Emily Asquith for the chance to claim a medal.

Sweeney was beaten 4-1 by Italian Chiara Mosetti in her last-16 bout after losing the final two rounds.

The Giants' starting cornerbacks are likely to be Greg Newsome and rookie second-round pick Colton Hood.

articles.title: Coach Rosenior taunts fans of former club who 'insulted my family' as Paris FC beats Strasbourg
articles.summary: After beating his former club to stay unbeaten in the French league on Saturday, Paris FC coach Liam Rosenior sparked a brief melee on the field by brazenly...
articles.body:
PARIS (AP) — After beating his former club to stay unbeaten in the French league on Saturday, Paris FC coach Liam Rosenior sparked a brief melee on the field by brazenly celebrating in front of the traveling Strasbourg fans.

Rosenior upset Strasbourg fans after leaving in January for a short and ill-fated spell at Chelsea . Near the end of Saturday's game, the stadium announcer asked visiting Strasbourg fans to stop aggressive chanting about Rosenior.

After the final whistle, Rosenior appeared to goad Strasbourg's fans, patting his chest and then spreading his arms out as he celebrated the victory. Some pushing and shoving then followed between both sets of players.

"A small section of the fans, and I want to stress that it was only a small section, because Strasbourg is a fantastic club, were disrespectful," Rosenior said. "They insulted my family. My bench was very angry. So, for me, celebrating like that was obviously sending a message. I won't say anything more about this."

The win kept his side undefeated after five league games.

articles.title: Czechs beat USA to qualify for Davis Cup finals
articles.summary: Jiri Lehecka downed Learner Tien in a deciding rubber as the Czech Republic stunned the United States 3-2 in Davis Cup qualifying for a second straight year,...
articles.body:
Jiri Lehecka downed Learner Tien in a deciding rubber as the Czech Republic stunned the United States 3-2 in Davis Cup qualifying for a second straight year, while South Korea reached the last eight for the first time on Saturday.

The Czechs knocked out the Americans at the same second qualifying round stage in a deciding rubber in Delray Beach a year ago, when Jakub Mensik beat Frances Tiafoe to secure a surprise victory.

Tomas Berdych's men repeated the feat in similarly dramatic fashion, to the delight of a raucous home crowd in Prague, as Lehecka clinched a 6-3, 7-5 win over world number 13 Tien.

The USA are record 32-time winners of the competition but their wait for a first title since 2007 goes on.

The Czechs advance to the November eight-team finals in Bologna, where hosts Italy will bid for a fourth straight title.

After starting the day locked at 1-1, the USA nudged ahead as Christian Harrison and Austin Krajicek saved four match points to outlast Adam Pavlasek and Patrik Rikl in a thrilling 5-7, 6-3, 7-6 (10/8) win.

Mensik then fought back from a set down to keep the tie alive by defeating recent US Open runner-up Ben Shelton 5-7, 6-4, 6-3.

Shelton took a tense first set after saving a set point when trailing 5-4, reeling off the last three games.

Mensik created a set point at exactly the same stage of the second, but this time made no mistake with a booming forehand to level the match.

The 21-year-old, a semi-finalist at this year's French Open, forced the tie into a deciding rubber on his second match point in a tense final game.

Lehecka, who beat Shelton in straight sets on Friday, recovered after giving an early break back to take the first set.

Tien forged 3-0 ahead as he attempted to force the tie all the way to a final set, but fell away and Lehecka clinched a brilliant win on his fourth match point.

Earlier, South Korea made history by beating India 3-1 in Seoul.

Kwon Soon-woo brushed Sumit Nagal aside 6-1, 6-2 to clinch the decisive point for the Koreans, who won both of Friday's singles rubbers before India triumphed in the doubles.

"I feel very proud for my country and every team I play against, I give my best," said Kwon. "When I play in a team, I know that I can't let my teammates down."

Austria also booked their spot as Jurij Rodionov sealed a 3-1 win for the hosts in Vienna with a 7-6 (8/6), 6-3 victory over Zizou Bergs, Belgium's number one in the absence of Alexander Blockx.

"I feel amazing. Proud of myself and the team. Big goal for us was to qualify to the Final 8," said Rodionov.

Rodionov got Austria on the board in Friday's opening singles before Bergs pulled Belgium level.

Doubles pair Lucas Miedler and Neil Oberleitner then beat Sander Gille and Joran Vliegen in straight sets to put Austria back on top.

France kept their tie with Canada alive, as Benjamin Bonzi and Pierre-Hugues Herbert beat Felix Auger-Aliassime and Duncan Chan in straight sets in the second day's opening doubles match to cut their deficit to 2-1.

Newly-crowned US Open champion Alexander Zverev gave Germany a 1-0 lead over Croatia in Halle, making a quick return to action as he beat Matej Dodig 6-4, 7-6 (7/3).

But Germany, who have not won the Davis Cup since 1993, were pegged back to end the first day level as Croatian youngster Dino Prizmic brushed aside Daniel Altmaier 6-4, 6-3.

Spain continued their tilt at a seventh title by seizing a 2-0 lead over Chile in Santiago courtesy of singles wins for Daniel Merida and Davis Cup debutant Rafael Jodar over Alejandro Tabilo and Cristian Garin, respectively.

Britain's Toby Samuel overcame Andres Andrade of Ecuador and Wimbledon semi-finalist Arthur Fery saw off Alvaro Guillen Meza as the hosts took a 2-0 advantage in London.

articles.title: Ashcraft’s Stellar First Full Season for Pirates Ends on IL; No Long-Term Concern
articles.summary: PITTSBURGH – Braxton Ashcraft’s stellar first extended season for the Pirates is over. The right-hander was placed on the 15-day […]
articles.body:
PITTSBURGH – Braxton Ashcraft 's stellar first extended season for the Pirates is over. The right-hander was placed on the 15-day injured list on Sep. 10 with right arm discomfort and will not return to the mound by the end of the year.

Fortunately for Ashcraft, who has an extensive injury history from his time as a prospect, his current arm discomfort is not anything to worry about long-term. He even said he would have pushed through it had the Pirates not been eliminated from the playoffs .

"I was never concerned," Ashcraft said of his injury. "Nobody ever had a concern about anything being structural or anything that was more than just general discomfort because of fatigue."

The general arm fatigue that has Ashcraft sidelined is something that came on rather abruptly. For most of the season, he felt good physically.

"It was one of those things that kind of presented all of a sudden," he explained. "It's part of the game. It's part of learning. It's part of going into your first full year with a true workload and learning how to manage that. I feel like the entire year, I did a really good job of that. I was never sore all year long. Just all of a sudden kind of bit me in the butt."

For much of the season, Ashcraft had been the team's most dependable starting pitcher. He made 28 starts and finished 14-6 with a 3.65 ERA. In 165.1 innings, he allowed 145 hits, walked 35 and struck out 173 batters. Ashcraft, who was named a National League All-Star, can be proud of the season he had.

"That's our goal, right, to be able to contribute to winning baseball games, and building a foundation here to create a winning culture … That's been my goal for my entire career, to be able to go out and post every time my name's on the sheet," he explained. " A big piece of that is going out and being able to cover your innings, and that's one thing I took a lot of pride in this year."

Ashcraft had a few memorable stats this season, including throwing a complete game shutout against the Marlins on Aug. 13. He also had two games in which he recorded double-digit strikeouts without walking a batter – once against the Twins on May 31 and another on June 24 against the Mariners .

But for Ashcraft, it's the starts that didn't go as well that still stand out to him.

"There were a couple games where I didn't quite do that or live up to what I expect of myself, and those kind of haunt me a little bit. But again, it's a learning experience. I'm grateful that I was able to come in this year and be able to do what I did."

While Ashcraft joked about trying to convince the medical staff to let him return, the 26-year-old will now look towards getting ready for the 2027 season. Throwing from 90 feet at PNC Park on Friday was the first step of that.

With a successful first full season in the big leagues, Ashcraft's focus will be to build off what he accomplished the next time he's back on the mound for the Pirates.

"I felt great throwing," he said. "I just need to get ready to begin next year in a better spot than I ended this year."

articles.body:
49ers tight end Jake Tonges 's final play of the 2026 season was a painful one in more ways than one.

The NFL announced that Tonges was fined $9,266 for unnecessary roughness in last week's win over the Rams. The fine was for an unpenalized leg whip block on Rams defensive end Myles Garrett in the second quarter.

articles.title: Georgia Tech beats Mercer 44-11
articles.summary: Jackets enter the win column
articles.body:
It wasn't the game we wanted it to happen in, but Georgia Tech (1-2) recorded its first win of the 2026 season beating the Mercer Bears 44-11.

Quarterback Alberto Mendoza threw for 249 yards with three touchdowns on 15-21 passing. Justice Haynes accounted for two rushing touchdowns with 141 rushing yards. Chad Alexander scored a touchdown as well.

On the whole, Tech did not look overly impressive given the context of this game. The line of scrimmage on both sides got pushed around early in the game and the defense certainly was not lockdown by any means. For most of the game, Mercer averaged more yards per carry than Tech and finished with 4.1 yards/carry to Tech's 3.9 yards/carry.

Tech was without plenty of starters, so backups got plenty of reps that did not get regular playing time in the first two games, which seemed to be a part of why Tech did not look solid early in the game.

On the good side, Mendoza when he threw looked solid and was hitting open receivers in the right spots. Jaivon Plummer caught a lovely pass in stride towards the end of the first half.

Tech goes to the west coast for their first game next week against a "new" ACC school since the entrance of Stanford/Cal/SMU out in Palo Alto to face the Cardinal.

Tech's line did not impress to start the game, nearly allowing a sack on the first play on a screen pass and failing to get a first down on the drive. After Mercer went three and out, Tech got their act together with a 26 yard completion to Dalen Penson and 25 yard pass to Justice Haynes to set up a 4 yard touchdown pass to Haynes.

After a second three and out, Tech's defense forced a turnover on a sack fumble recovered by Christian Speakman to give Tech the ball in Mercer territory.

A Dalen Penson catch brought Tech to goal to go from the six yard line, then the one after a Malachi Hosley run that was initially ruled a touchdown but overturned on review. Second and goal wasn't punched in by Hosley. Third and goal saw an overthrow of Chris Corbo by Alberto Mendoza. Finally on fourth and goal, Justice Haynes punched it in for a 14-0 lead.

Mercer's next drive was the kind we were worried Tech would allow. The line play was bad, allowing multiple runs that made first downs a formality. Unnecessary penalties gave the Bears two additional first downs. At goal to go, Mercer had scored out of a timeout where Tech was not ready on the snap before a quick review showed the runner was out of bounds at the 1. Thankfully, Mercer's play call on 3rd & goal was a delayed QB run that Tech easily snuffed to force a field goal to make it 14-3.

Tech's drive by some miracle didn't end four different ways. After a first downs from Dalen Penson, Haynes, and Kevin Roche, Tech was in the redzone and about to get bailed out multiple different ways. On 4th & inches, a botched play turned into a first down on an offsides penalty. On third & 6 from the 11, Mendoza had scrambled in for a TD but was called back for holding. The proceeding 3rd & 16 play resulted defensive pass interference, giving Tech 1st & goal at the two yard line. After two attempts to punch it in failed, 3rd & goal from the one yard line was moved to the six after a snap infraction penalty, and then Mendoza got sacked. Tech settled for a field goal to go up 17-3.

After a Mercer punt, Tech hit the "explosive" button for the first time all season, needing only a 23 yard catch by Kevin Roche, Jr. and a 37 yard touchdown catch by Jaiven Plummer to go up 24-3 before the end of the half.

Mercer turned to J.P. Pickles at quarterback in the second half, and he gashed Tech for multiple first down runs, but Tech was able to hold the Bears outside the redzone to force a field goal to make it 24-6.

Tech gave the keys to Justice Haynes on their next drive, starting with a 20 yard run and finishing with a 31 yard touchdown score. On the ensuing PAT, Aidan Birr was blocked and the kick was returned for a two point safety to make it 30-8.

Pickles again was able to move the ball for Mercer, connecting with Brayden Smith for 37 yards and Jackson Kostmayer to get in the red zone. A holding penalty and Brayden Manley/Tawfiq Thomas sack forced the drive to end with a field goal to make it 30-11.

After a long return from Chad Alexander to start Tech's next drive at their own 48, Tech quickly scored on a 33 yard Debron Gatling touchdown catch to make it 37-11.

If we weren't in garbage time already, the game reached that point when freshman linebacker C.J. Gamble picked off Mercer to start the fourth quarter. Tech reached goal to go after a Tre Maddox first down catch was added on by a roughing the passer penalty. Chad Alexander got the score from one yard out to make it 44-11.

articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino backs Bayern Munich star Harry Kane to win the Ballon d’Or
articles.summary: The FC Bayern’s former coach at Tottenham Hotspur thinks he deserves to win the Ballon d’Or
articles.body:
The Harry Kane Ballon d'Or hype train is packed and it's not showing signs of slowing down any time soon. The latest name to voice his support for the 33-year-old England star is USMNT coach Mauricio Pochettino, who coached Kane at Tottenham Hotspur .

"My wish, I hope yes. I think he deserves it as the reward for his career and for all what he has done in football," Pochettino said on Sky Sports (as captured by X account @iMiaSanMia ). "I don't know if he is going to be punished for the World Cup or the Champions League because he played in both semifinals. Maybe he will be punished, I don't know, but, for me, it's Harry Kane's time. I think he deserves it. He deserves it in his career like Modrić , Cannavaro or Benzema . I think if I pick one, then it's Harry Kane."

With Kane letting his football do the talking instead of spouting unsupported claims in the media on who should win the Ballon d'Or and with high-profile individuals supporting his cause, there's no reason why he shouldn't win it.

articles.title: WWE fans could be about to get their Cody Rhodes wish as Triple H drops backstage footage
articles.summary: WWE fans have had a great run with Cody Rhodes as the babyface of the company but things could be about to change. Rhodes has very much led WWE into the new...
articles.body:
WWE fans have had a great run with Cody Rhodes as the babyface of the company but things could be about to change.

Rhodes has very much led WWE into the new era alongside Roman Reigns and he's earned the nickname 'QB1' for a reason.

However, with so much talent on the roster now and a lot of babyfaces in there as well, there have been multiple calls from fans to see Rhodes go rogue and turn full heel.

Recent weeks have given up glimpses into how Rhodes the heel would work while those who saw his run in AEW will know exactly what he brings to the table.

Now, it looks like we've stepped ever closer.

Cody Rhodes teases heel turn in interview with Michael Cole

WWE are doing a great job at the moment of putting different aspects of their product across different platforms.

With Rhodes doing an interview with Michael Cole for Smackdown last night, it seemed it was the usual shtick from Rhodes towards Randy Orton.

However, Triple H then shared fresh footage of the interview ending where Rhodes whispered to Cole that 'If it happens again, I'm going to kick his f——- head off'.

The story with Orton is very much building and continuing organically.

There is no need for any sort of title involvement and the story is basically already there for both Rhodes and Orton to work with.

The payoff is coming soon and whether or not we see Rhodes finally take that dark turn, or we see WWE use it as a way to suggest Rhodes will never go down that path, remains to be seen.

articles.title: Super League play-offs: Dates, format, schedule as Wigan, Leeds, Wakefield, Warrington vie for spot in Grand Final at Old Trafford

articles.body:
Wigan Warriors emphatically wrapped up a domestic double with a 50-12 win over Catalans Dragons to secure the League Leaders' Shield.

That adds to their Challenge Cup win and now they are on the hunt for the treble if they can win in 'the big dance' at the Grand Final.

Four remain and now we will whittle it down to the two teams who will do battle to win the trophy everyone has been hunting.

The format now is simple. Third-place finisher Warrington beat Hull KR who came sixth. Fourth-placed Wakefield beat fifth-placed finisher Leigh for a spot in the semi-finals on Friday.

The lowest-ranked winner of those contests, so the team that finished lowest in the league table, take on Wigan Warriors. After Warrington's win, that means Wakefield will head to the home of the League Leaders' Shield winners.

articles.title: Manchester United Women denied at death after superb display against Arsenal
articles.summary: 1Manchester United were denied a superb victory at the Emirates Stadium as Smilla Holmberg’s 95th-minute equaliser rescued a 1-1 draw for Arsenal.Julia Zigio...
articles.body:
Manchester United were denied a superb victory at the Emirates Stadium as Smilla Holmberg's 95th-minute equaliser rescued a 1-1 draw for Arsenal .

Julia Zigiotti Olme had given Eva Olid's side a second-half lead, only for Holmberg to convert at the back post with virtually the final meaningful action. Even so, United's first point under their new head coach represented an emphatic response to two difficult opening defeats.

The Red Devils arrived in north London under pressure following losses against London City Lionesses and Chelsea . Having conceded five goals in their previous fixture, another demanding afternoon appeared likely against Arsenal .

Olid's players instead produced a disciplined, defiant performance. Phallon Tullis-Joyce started behind a defensive unit containing Maya Le Tissier , Dominique Janssen and Anna Sandberg , while Zigiotti Olme and Hinata Miyazawa provided protection in midfield.

Jess Park and Simi Awujo were also included, with Elisabeth Terland leading the line. United spent long periods without the ball but retained enough threat to stop Arsenal committing everybody forward without consequence.

Arsenal made the brighter start and tested Tullis-Joyce through Lisa Baum. Mariona Caldentey then curled an effort narrowly wide as the hosts attempted to stretch United from both flanks.

Tullis-Joyce was required again shortly before half-time, producing a fine save to deny Stina Blackstenius ' header. The goalkeeper's handling and positioning helped United survive Arsenal's strongest spells.

However, the clearest United opening fell to Terland. The striker was denied twice in quick succession by Misa Rodríguez, offering an important warning that the visitors could create chances despite Arsenal controlling more of the possession.

The breakthrough arrived after a costly mistake from Georgia Stanway . Her attempted pass towards Steph Catley rolled into Zigiotti Olme's path, leaving the United midfielder with an unexpected route to goal.

Zigiotti Olme kept her composure, moved around Catley and finished through Rodríguez's legs. It was a clinical piece of punishment from a player alert enough to anticipate the error.

United then had to withstand sustained pressure. Tullis-Joyce saved well from Caitlin Foord , while Olid's defenders repeatedly cleared dangerous deliveries and dealt with a succession of Arsenal set-pieces.

Rebecca Bernal replaced Awujo early in the second half, with Lea Schüller later coming on for Terland. Those changes gave United fresh legs as the match became an increasingly determined exercise in protecting their narrow advantage.

The resistance held until the fifth minute of added time. Leah Williamson sent a deep diagonal ball into the area and substitute Holmberg arrived at the back post to score, leaving United's players on their knees after coming so close to victory.

The statistics recorded on BBC Sport underline the scale of the visitors' defensive effort. Arsenal had 60 per cent possession, 17 attempts and 12 corners, compared with United's four attempts and no corners.

Zigiotti Olme supplied the decisive attacking contribution and remained composed when Arsenal's error presented the opportunity. Her finish ensured United's work without the ball was rewarded rather than merely admirable.

Tullis-Joyce was equally important. Her saves from Blackstenius and Foord kept the Red Devils ahead, while Terland's first-half openings showed that United carried a genuine counter-attacking threat.

Le Tissier, Janssen and Sandberg played central roles in a collective rearguard action. Although the late goal was painful, the organisation and commitment were a marked improvement from United's opening two matches.

Olid will naturally be disappointed that her side could not survive the final delivery, but this was a valuable point and a performance upon which she can build. The task now is to retain that defensive resilience while finding a way to exert more control with the ball.

United earned their first point under Eva Olid.

Julia Zigiotti Olme scored the visitors' goal.

Phallon Tullis-Joyce made several important saves.

Smilla Holmberg equalised in the 95th minute.
