articles.title: Cowboys vs Commanders: Writer predictions for Week 2
articles.summary: Do you think the Cowboys are going to take care of business this week?
articles.body:
Week 2 brings the Dallas Cowboys home for a divisional matchup with the Washington Commanders , and both teams enter with plenty to correct from opening weekend. With key injuries, new-look defenses and several important individual matchups likely to shape the game, here is what to expect when each offense has the football and some predictions from our BTB staff.

Washington should look at what the Giants did to Dallas in Week 1 and follow a similar plan which is run the football, keep the Cowboys guessing and make Jayden Daniels part of the rushing attack. The Commanders produced 132 rushing yards against Philadelphia , with Jacory Croskey-Merritt gaining 63 yards on 16 carries and Daniels adding 31 yards.

Daniels only threw for 164 yards, but he finished with two touchdowns and no interceptions and became much more effective late in the game. The Cowboys, meanwhile, surrendered 165 rushing yards to New York and allowed the Giants to convert nine of 11 third downs. Even more concerning was Dallas' inability to create pressure without sending extra defenders. When the Cowboys rushed four, they generated only two pressures, and Jaxson Dart completed 17 of 19 passes for 200 yards and two touchdowns on those plays.

The route to victory for Washington is patience. Dallas wants its expensive defensive front to attack, but Daniels can use that aggression against them with option runs, screens and using his shifty movement outside the pocket. If they establish the run early and force Dallas' linebackers and safeties (both positions suffered injuries last week) to communicate correctly on every snap, there are opportunities for explosive plays.

Dallas needs a much better offensive start than it produced against New York. The Cowboys finished Week 1 with only 244 total yards, Dak Prescott threw for 175 yards and Javonte Williams managed only 41 rushing yards on 12 carries. The offensive line kept Prescott from being sacked, but it struggled to create movement in the running game, particularly early.

That presents an interesting matchup because Washington's redesigned defense looked considerably faster and more aggressive against Philadelphia. New defensive coordinator Daronte Jones mixed his fronts, pressures and coverages, and the Commanders recorded three sacks, including one each from Odafe Oweh and rookie Sonny Styles .

Dallas should not simply line up and repeatedly run into that front, especially with Tyler Smith still on injured reserve and T.J. Bass starting at left guard. The better plan is to make Washington defend the whole field. Quick throws to CeeDee Lamb , George Pickens and Jake Ferguson can slow down the blitz, while screens and play-action can punish linebackers for attacking too aggressively.

There are also big plays available. Philadelphia gained 318 yards against Washington, but roughly half of those yards came on only four plays, including completions of 64 and 31 yards. Washington played good defense for long periods but suffered costly coverage mistakes. That is exactly where Lamb and Pickens should become the focus.

The Cowboys still need Javonte Williams involved because becoming one-dimensional will allow Washington to attack Prescott. But Dallas should use the run to create opportunities rather than making it the entire plan. Williams averaged only 3.4 yards per carry in Week 1, while Washington generally controlled Saquon Barkley outside of one 42-yard run. Getting Williams involved as a receiver could be particularly useful against Washington's pressure packages.

Now onto the predictions from your BTB writers…

I will admit to possibly overreacting, but I'm not feeling very positive about the Cowboys bouncing back. Too many questions, too many problems, no clear answers in sight. I'm afraid Dallas will slump to 0-2 by a score of WAS 27 DAL 23

The Cowboys got punched in the mouth by the New York Giants and were humbled in a big apple kind of way. Luckily they should have the leadership in the locker room to steady the ship and shift their focus to a must win matchup at home against the Washington Commanders.

Dallas underestimated New York in the ground game so hopefully they don't fall for the same mistake vs Washington. Dallas should bounce back in their own backyard, but it'll be a grudge match considering both teams want to avoid 0-2.

Cowboys win by the skin of their teeth 23-20.

The game turned on its head when George Pickens dropped the deep ball last week against the Giants. That won't happen twice. Pickens and the offense gets rolling at home while the defense takes a small but important step forward against the Commanders. DAL 27 WAS 20

Falling to 0-2 is basically the kiss of death for your playoff hopes, so both teams are going to come into this game with plenty of desperation. The Cowboys are a better team than they showed last Sunday night. Will the better version show up against Washington? While I don't see the defense getting much better, I do see Dallas' high-powered offense firing on all cylinders in the home opener. Week 2 in Dallas is a shootout once again as the Cowboys escape with a victory. Give me Dallas, 36-31.

Dak Prescott has never lost at home to Washington and is 7-0. As Washington they have to play their second consecutive road game to a division rival, and last week's loss puts them huge pressure to come out here. A lot of starters didn't play a great deal, if at all during preseason so last week was pretty much their dress rehearsal. Let's see the adjustment on defense and get the win column started.

articles.title: Puka Nacua questionable for Rams’ home opener; Aaron Donald expected to play
articles.summary: WOODLAND HILLS, Calif.
articles.body:
WOODLAND HILLS, Calif. — The Rams could be without Puka Nacua for their Monday night home opener, with coach Sean McVay saying Saturday that the wide receiver would miss practice and be listed as questionable as the team monitors his injury.

McVay initially identified Nacua's injury as a hip issue before describing soreness in his groin that has affected his ability to reach full speed. He said the injury is separate from the psoas issue Nacua dealt with during training camp and that a decision on his availability remains pending.

"He's got a little bit of soreness in that groin," McVay said. "Being smart with him as a skill player. Whether or not he plays is to be determined and so we'll see how he's feeling, but he won't practice today."

Nacua participated in Thursday's practice, but McVay said the receiver did not feel entirely like himself. That prompted the Rams to take a cautious approach over the following days as they prepared for their first game at SoFi Stadium this season.

"He felt good but didn't feel totally like himself, his ability to be able to open up and really hit full speed," McVay said. "So he had some soreness in there and so that's why we've been smart with him the last couple days."

The uncertainty surrounding Nacua comes as the Rams face another potential absence at receiver. Jordan Whittington is doubtful with a quadriceps injury, leaving Los Angeles preparing for the possibility of having both players unavailable Monday.

The Rams will also be without safety Kam Kinchens , whom McVay ruled out with a hamstring injury. Safety Kam Curl and inside linebacker Nate Landman were listed as limited for Saturday's practice, while inside linebacker Omar Speights was listed as a full participant. McVay said the other players sitting out for rest would be ready for the game.

While Nacua's status remains unsettled, McVay offered a more encouraging update on Aaron Donald , who is expected to play Monday following his return from retirement.

Donald said Friday that the plan was for him to play. Asked about that assessment, McVay left little room for doubt.

"If he said it, he's going," McVay said. "Whatever Aaron says, I support. He's been awesome."

Donald's availability carries added significance with outside linebacker Myles Garrett on injured reserve. McVay reiterated that Garrett's surgery went well and said the Rams look forward to his return, but Donald has already given the team a boost.

"He's definitely provided a spark for us, and you can see there's a lot of love that his teammates have for him and a lot of respect and admiration just by how he carries himself," McVay said.

For McVay, Donald's influence extends beyond his work on the field. The coach pointed to the veteran's example and the attention he commands from teammates as qualities that can help the Rams navigate Garrett's absence.

"When he speaks, everybody listens," McVay said. "But more importantly like I was mentioning earlier, he just models the way."

The Rams are eager to return to competition after their season-opening loss and an extended wait for another opportunity. Asked how long the stretch between games has felt, McVay answered, "An eternity."

He said the focus is on applying what the team learned from the opener to its preparation, coaching and execution Monday night.

"Let's go swing. Let's go for it," McVay said. "Let's apply some of the things that we learned to try to be able to have a better outcome in terms of what we're looking for, our style of play, the way we coach and things like that."

Now in his 10th season, McVay said the anticipation of a home opener remains strong. The Rams will have to balance that excitement with uncertainty over Nacua's availability as they finish preparing for Monday.

"SoFi is a great atmosphere and environment," McVay said. "I love our fans, excited to hear them try to impact that game for us in a positive way."

articles.title: Olid's Man Utd take big step forward after 'intense week'
articles.summary: A week ago, the picture at Manchester United looked bleak. Then on Saturday, victory was snatched away from them at Arsenal. But have we seen signs of improv...
articles.body:
A week ago, the picture for Manchester United looked a lot bleaker than it did at the full-time whistle on Saturday.

Regardless of the stoppage-time equaliser they conceded at Arsenal 's Emirates Stadium, United's performance marked a major sign of progress.

Defeats in their opening two matches, including a 5-0 thrashing by Chelsea , meant the list of questions for new manager Eva Olid seemed endless.

United were disorganised, lacking in identity and were wide open at the back as their new era under Olid began in disappointing fashion.

Those early displays did little to fill supporters with confidence, and Olid faced criticism for her decisions despite being in the job just a matter of weeks.

However, a gutsy defensive display against Arsenal delivered a well-earned 1-1 draw and they were only denied victory by a 95th-minute leveller.

While United's wait for a first Women's Super League win of the season continues, this performance suggested there may not be quite the cause for concern many suspected.

Olid, 41, took over as manager in the summer, joining from Hearts, and promised to implement a new attacking style of play that focused heavily on possession.

However, in their opening two games, United had just two shots on target and less than 40% possession in both matches. In the second of those games, they suffered the five-goal humbling at home by Chelsea.

Few expected them to come away with anything against an Arsenal team who many tipped to win the title before the season kicked off, albeit they have struggled to score goals efficiently.

Olid knew it would be a test but said on Friday she wanted her players to believe in themselves, show confidence, and to go back to the defensive roots they knew and built so well under her predecessor Marc Skinner.

"It has been an intense week because there were a lot of emotions from players and staff. Nobody wants to lose 5-0," said Olid.

"We grew as a team. The first day after losing 5-0 is not easy for anyone. We spoke and said we needed energy this week and a positive mindset.

"The focus was the defensive shape. It's trying to get them more confidence."

Olid ultimately wants her United team to dominate the ball and create more chances in front of goal, but this time they delivered on her plea to be defensively solid.

They looked well organised in an even first half in which United midfielder Simi Awujo stood out, while Andrea Medina tracked back effectively.

They won more duels than Arsenal, put in more tackles and completed more interceptions than their opponents - but still had only 40% of possession.

Former England midfielder Izzy Christiansen told Sky Sports: "Manchester United have done a terrific job defensively. Overall, it's just been solid.

"It looks so much better. The addition of Awujo has added some running power and they look so much freer in the final third."

Arsenal's pressure grew in an edgy second half, but United held on for as long as they could and were unfortunate to concede with seconds left on the clock.

They had led from midway through the half, after Julia Zigiotti seized on a mistake from Georgia Stanway .

Smilla Holmberg's late volley denied United the spoils, but Olid saw foundations she could build on.

"I think the attacking will come," she said. "If you implement a new style of play, you need time.

"That effort, that intensity, can never be missed. We deserved three points for the hard work and the effort.

"Of course, we need to create more chances. That is why I'm here. We need time, but today is the minimum that we have to deliver. I hope we can improve the attacking side."

The biggest question is whether United really can build on this performance.

They were already a difficult team to break down under Skinner but came up short in previous big games against WSL title rivals.

In three Women's FA Cup finals, United won once against Tottenham , falling to higher-placed Chelsea on the other two occasions.

Four years have passed since they won a game at Emirates Stadium against Arsenal, and their heavy defeat by Chelsea last week showed the gap to the elite still remains.

Olid was brought in to transform their style by implementing an attacking philosophy that the club hope will deliver them long-term success.

Patience was already beginning to wane after their demoralising early defeats, so conversations took place and they had to revert back to what they already knew.

The result of that is significant progress from last week, but is it progress for the long term?

"We are a team who need to press high, but at the same time we want to be better with the ball," Olid said on Sky Sports.

"We lose simple passes and we cannot recognise the free player. Those things need to improve. It will come, I'm sure.

"But we need to keep this [defensive structure], then from there, little by little, be an attacking team, create more chances, score more goals.

"I cannot pretend it's happening in four weeks, but I'm sure it will come."

articles.title: Fulham vs Manchester United: Premier League – prediction, teams, lineups
articles.summary: Man United have won only one league game this season, putting Michael Carrick under pressure ahead of Fulham trip.
articles.body:
Who: Fulham vs Manchester United What: English Premier League Where: Craven Cottage, London in United Kingdom When: Sunday, September 20, at 4:30pm (15:30 GMT) How to follow: Al Jazeera Sport will have all the build-up to our live text commentary stream from 12:30 GMT.

One month into the new ‌Premier League season, excuses about bedding-in processes and newly assembled squads needing time to gel are wearing thin and for Manchester United ⁠there is an acute sense ⁠of urgency as the international break looms.

United are by no means the only ‘big club’ enduring a faltering start to the campaign but after so much pre-season optimism, the spotlight has fallen very much on manager Michael Carrick ahead of ⁠Sunday’s trip to Fulham.

Al Jazeera takes a closer look at the game:

How have Manchester United started the new season?

United have ⁠lost three of their six matches in all competitions and suffered a damaging League Cup exit on Wednesday, surrendering a 2-0 ⁠lead to Brighton & Hove Albion.

Their only win in four league games came at home to promoted Ipswich Town.

United started the better in the VAR-dominated Manchester derby last Sunday, but played second fiddle to the away team after City were reduced to ten men.

The London club have made a slow start under new manager Alvaro Arbeloa and are yet to win in the league.

A draw at Liverpool last week and a League Cup win at West Ham United in midweek offered glimpses of better things to come.

What has Carrick said about United’s start to the season?

Carrick accepted responsibility for the team’s poor start but said the focus must remain on finding ⁠solutions rather than assigning blame.

“It’s my responsibility and I’m fine with that. It’s not a blame ⁠game. Blame me, no problem, but it’s ⁠not about blaming people,” said the 45-year-old boss.

“It’s about finding solutions. It’s a whole collective thing. It’s about what you focus on. I know where we want to get to ‌and we want to get there fast.”

What happened the last time Fulham played Man Utd?

United won 3-2 in their last meeting which came in the Premier League at Old Trafford on February 1.

Casemiro and Matheus Cunha put United two up before a chaotic finale that saw Raul Jiminez net an 85th minute penalty for the Londoners before Benjamin Sesko and Kevin traded injury time strikes.

What happened between Fulham and Man Utd at Craven Cottage last season?

The teams shared a 1-1 draw in the Premier League match. Emile Smith Rowe’s 73rd minute goal levelled matters after Rodrigo Muniz put through his own net in the 58th minute.

When did Fulham last beat Manchester United?

Fulham won 2-1 at Old Trafford in the Premier League on February 24, 2024. Harry Maguire appeared to have sealed a point for United in the 90th minute when he cancelled out Calvin Bassey’s 65th minute goal, but Alex Iwobi got Fulham’s winner in injury time.

United have won three of the five meetings since then.

When did Fulham last beat Man Utd at Craven Cottage?

Fulham have not recorded a home win against United since December 2009. Danny Murphy, Bobby Zamora and Damien Duff sealing a 3-0 home win.

Of the 10 matches since then, United have won nine, scoring 21 and conceding six.

Opta’s supercomputer has given Manchester United a 47.4 percent chance of winning, while offering Fulham only a 28.3 percent chance of victory.

This will be their 94th meeting, with Manchester United winning 59 of the encounters and Fulham 14.

articles.title: World Series of Darts Finals 2026 results: Luke Littler beats Nathan Aspinall 10-9 to reach quarter-finals
articles.summary: World champion Luke Littler beats Nathan Aspinall 10-9 to reach the last eight of the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam.
articles.body:
World champion Luke Littler beat Nathan Aspinall in a dramatic finale to reach the last eight of the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam.

Littler, 19, trailed 9-8 in a best-of-19 contest that had been close throughout and he held throw in the 18th leg to force a decider.

Needing to break Aspinall's throw to win, Littler started the leg with his seventh 180 of the match and checked out 58 for a match-clinching 12-darter.

The two Englishmen had been involved in a World Matchplay classic in July, when Littler threw a nine-darter in the opening leg of an 11-8 victory.

"The pace of the game suits us both, we're good friends and we bring the best out of each other," said Littler, who has a chance to complete a clean sweep of the PDC's premier events in 2026.

"I only played well in the last session [from 6-6 onwards]. In the first two sessions, I didn't feel confident but I managed to get it to 6-6 and I was very good in the third."

The world number one will meet former Premier League champion Jonny Clayton in the quarter-finals on Sunday.

Clayton beat Japan's Motomu Sakai 10-8 and is one of two Welshmen in the last eight, with Gerwyn Price also progressing courtesy of a 10-5 win against Canada's Jim Long.

England's James Wade was the other winner in Saturday's evening session, defeating Wessel Nijman of the Netherlands, and will face Price next.

Littler survives scare to progress in Amsterdam

Champion Van Gerwen loses in first round to Gurney

Earlier on Saturday, world number two Luke Humphries lost the deciding leg of his last-16 match against Dirk van Duijvenbode.

Van Duijvenbode's next opponent will be fellow Dutchman Gian van Veen, who was beaten by Littler in January's World Championship final.

articles.summary: Luke 'The Nuke' Littler will win his first clean sweep of majors in one year if he wins the World Series of Darts on Sunday; he will take on Jonny Clayton in the quarter-finals after a dramatic second-round victory over Nathan Aspinall; Luke Humphries crashed out to Dirk van Duijvenbode
articles.body:
Littler, the 2024 champion who was beaten 11-7 by Michael van Gerwen in last year's final, edged out Aspinall 10-9 in the World Series of Darts Finals second round, taking the last two legs in a see-saw contest and sealing victory with a 12-dart break.

Following the win in the Dutch capital, Littler said: "Nathan pushed me all the way tonight; I didn't feel confident in the first two sessions, but I managed to make it 6-6 and I was very good in the final session.

"When I came here two years ago, Ross Smith missed darts to beat me and then I went on to win the title, but I know it will be a good test against Jonny (Clayton) tomorrow (Sunday).

"I'm glad that the streak is still on, but it's going to be very tough."

Earlier on Saturday, Gerwyn Price defeated Jim Long 10-5 and James Wade saw off Wessel Nijman 10-7.

Luke Humphries crashed out with 10-9 defeat to Dirk van Duijvenbode, in the afternoon session, while Josh Rock secured a 10-7 win over Ryan Searle and Ross Smith beat Daryl Gurney 10-5.

An emotional Van Duijvenbode, who was joined by young son Levi on stage after the match, said: "Having my kid here is the best thing in my life.

"I won this game because he was here. When you are playing against the world number two you are always nervous.

"When I looked up at him he made so happy every time. It made me so relaxed. In the end that is the reason I won it."

Gian van Veen prevailed 10-7 against Karel Sedlacek and now faces Van Duijvenbode in an all-Dutch quarter-final, while Jonny Clayton battled past Motomu Sakai 10-8 to set up his showdown with Littler.

The semi-finals and final will take place from 6pm on Sunday, following the quarter-finals in the afternoon.

articles.title: Highlights, MVP, and Twitter reactions to Kentucky’s historic win vs. No. 9 Texas A&M
articles.summary: The Cats go into College Station and come away with a dominant win over 9th-ranked Texas A&M.
articles.body:
Kentucky Football traveled to College Station for a matchup with the No. 9 Texas A&M Aggies , with more on the line than a simple win or loss. Remaining competitive for four quarters was something every UK supporter was eager to see on Saturday afternoon.

Beating Texas A&M on the road in front of 102,000 screaming fans is a tall task for any program — let alone a first‑year head coach in just his third game ever.

That said, a stellar first-half performance last week against a top-10 Alabama team ignited optimism within the BBN and proved Stein's squad can play with anyone.

Much like last week, the Cats immediately jumped at the opportunity to show they can compete against a top‑tier SEC opponent. Two incredible defensive plays by Sam Greene allowed the defense to maintain control in a hostile environment for much of the first half. Credit to the Cats for coming out with enough juice to shake the A&M faithful.

It took the Aggies nearly 25 minutes to put points on the board on a 2-yard touchdown run. Kentucky responded with a score of their own, knotting it up 7-7 at the half.

Will Stein must have pressed all the right buttons in the locker room because the third quarter belonged to Kentucky. The Cats came out and dominated both sides of the ball, leaving patrons at Kyle Field stunned.

By the time the onslaught was complete, UK would enter the fourth quarter with a commanding 28-7 lead. That 15-minute stretch of football was about as good as it gets and will be remembered fondly.

The Aggies tried their best to mount a late comeback, but Kentucky was just too physical and simply outmatched A&M in every facet of the contest. At many times in the second half, UK fans found themselves grinning ear-to-ear and/or texting friends that they couldn't believe it was happening.

According to UK statistician Corey Price, this was Kentucky's second-largest margin of victory over a top-10 program in the modern era, as the last one came against Vanderbilt in 1947.

In addition, Will Stein becomes the first Kentucky Football coach to win a road game vs. a top-25 team in his first season at the school.

Despite a huge win over a top-10 team on the road, this was not an easy game to select a single player for MVP. The Cats managed to spread out the offensive production, and players like Sam Greene made their case to get the nod defensively. Heck, even special teams got in on the action with Adam Zouagui bouncing in an important 52-yard field goal late in the game.

But at the end of the day, it was UK quarterback Kenny Minchey who rose to the occasion and led his team to victory against a top-10 team in front of 102,000 hostile fans in College Station. It didn't take the Notre Dame transfer long to secure a signature win as a starting QB. Kentucky Football fans know all too well that convincing SEC road wins like we saw today are uncommon, making the win over the Aggies even more memorable.

Minchey's second-half execution was textbook and ensured his team never wavered after building a large lead. His final stats didn't jump off the page, but 252 yards and two touchdowns were more than enough to get the job done on the road.

If Kenny Minchey can remain poised like he did today, the sky could be the limit for this offense.

articles.title: Maiava throws for 277 yards and 2 TDs in No. 12 USC's 42-35 win at Rutgers
articles.summary: Jayden Maiava threw for 277 yards and two touchdowns and King Miller ran for 102 yards and a TD to help No. 12 Southern California beat Rutgers 42-35 on Satu...
articles.body:
PISCATAWAY, N.J. (AP) — Jayden Maiava threw for 277 yards and two touchdowns and King Miller ran for 102 yards and a TD to help No. 12 Southern California beat Rutgers 42-35 on Saturday in the Big Ten opener for both teams.

The Trojans (4-0) never trailed, building a 35-21 cushion with 5:52 left in the third quarter. Rutgers (0-3) closed to 35-28 in the quarter before the teams traded touchdowns in the fourth.

Trojans star freshman receiver Trent Mosley sat out with a knee injury. Fellow freshman Kayden Dixon-Wyatt had five catches for 77 yards.

Running back Riley Wormley ran for a TD and caught a touchdown pass that put USC ahead 42-28 with 3:04 to play.

Dylan Lonergan passed for 272 yards and three TDs for Rutgers.

The Trojans need to shore up their defense if they intend to compete with high-powered offenses like Oregon , Ohio State and Indiana. Southern Cal gave up five plays of 20 yards or more against Rutgers. In three games, USC has allowed its opponents to score 10 of 13 times in the red zone.

Rutgers has held a lead in just 2:54 this season when it scored on its opening drive in a 37-21 loss to UMass in the first game and never led against Boston College and USC. Turnovers continue to be a major issue. The Scarlet Knights have a -7 turnover margin after Lonergan's two picks Saturday, including a 99-yard interception by Prophet Brown for a TD.

articles.title: Eddie Hearn plots shocking switch to Team Chris Eubank Jr. ahead of Conor Benn trilogy
articles.summary: Eddie Hearn looks to hit back at Conor Benn and Dana White with Chris Eubank Jr. bombshell.

Eddie Hearn 's bad blood with Conor Benn and Dana White is no secret, but his latest move has shaken the entire boxing landscape.

The war between Hearn and White has been public for a long time. Both men have had their moments in the feud, with the UFC CEO likely pushing ahead after snatching prize fighter Conor Benn from under Hearn's nose. But if everything goes according to plan for the British promoter, he'll look to level the score and potentially one-up his rival.

In a significant promotional plot twist, Eddie Hearn revealed he had a pleasant lunch with Chris Eubank Jr., as he looks to bury the hatchet with an old foe.

"Look, stranger things have happened," Hearn said. "I will confirm that I had a very pleasant lunch meeting with Mr. Eubank. And it was nice. It was nice to clear the air a little bit."

Eddie Hearn unapologetically stood by Conor Benn during the media and fans' inquest into his performance-enhancing drugs scandal. But their relationship has since been torn apart , and it looks like Hearn wants to get back at Benn and Dana White.

With his sights set on a potential trilogy clash, Hearn hinted at potentially representing Chris Eubank Jr., saying:

"Certainly, me on Team Eubank against Dana White and Conor Benn makes the fight twice as big, and the trilogy will be interesting."

"But if I'm on Team Eubank, I'll make sure everything's fair this time. You know, I think Chris understands and appreciates that my job last time was to get the edge. And I did that beautifully. Because I spun the other team around my finger, and I enabled Conor Benn to get the advantage going into the fight. That's the game."

articles.title: Key observations from Wisconsin’s win over Eastern Michigan
articles.summary: The Badgers stood out in many ways on Saturday.
articles.body:
The Wisconsin Badgers blew out the Eastern Michigan Eagles 54-10 on Saturday, improving to 2-1 ahead of Big Ten play with a dominant victory.

The Badgers led 31-7 by halftime and didn't face any resistance in the second half, as they had 479 yards of offense, forced three turnovers, and stood out on special teams.

Here are all the key game notes and observations from Wisconsin's Week 3 win, courtesy of UW Athletics.

1. Today's captains: LB Aaron Witt, sophomore LB Mason Posa and sophomore LB Cooper Catalano.

2. Today's attendance at Camp Randall Stadium was 66,545.

3. Wisconsin's 54 points were the most since posting 66 points against New Mexico State on Sept. 17, 2022. UW's 44-point win was its largest since earning a 46-point win against Purdue on Oct. 5, 2024

5. The Badgers racked up 479 yards of offense, their most since posting 549 yards of offense against Rutgers on Oct. 12, 2024. Wisconsin has now posted 400+ yards of offense in back-to-back games for the first time since games against Purdue and Rutgers in October 2024.

6. The Badgers improved to 5-0 all time against Eastern Michigan. UW has outscored the Eagles 189-26 in the five meetings.

7. UW's 31 points scored in the first half were the most since UW had 35 points in a 66-7 win over New Mexico State on Sept. 17, 2022.

8. The Badgers went 8-of-12 on third down (66.7 percent) while holding the Eagles to 3-of-12 on third down (25.0 percent).

9. Wisconsin scored a defensive TD for the first time since Ricardo Hallman posted a 95-yard pick-six against Rutgers on Oct. 7, 2023. LB Cooper Catalano's scoop and score was Wisconsin's first fumble return for a TD since Matt Henningsen recorded one against Northwestern on Sept. 28, 2019.

10. Wisconsin forced 3 turnovers, earning a pair of interceptions and a forced fumble. It marks the first time UW has forced 3 turnovers in a single game since doing so against USC on Sept. 28, 2024.

11. UW ended the game blocking Eastern Michigan's 48-yard field goal attempt as CB Eric Fletcher Jr. blocked the kick and CB Donovan Dunmore returned it for the score. It marks the first time the Badgers blocked a field goal and returned it for a score since Reggie Cribbs blocked a field goal and Jim Leonhard returned it 86 yards for a score against UNLV on Sept. 11, 2004.

12. UW did not punt in the game, marking the first time since a 45-24 win vs. Purdue on Nov. 11, 2019 that the Badgers did not record a punt.

1. QB Colton Joseph completed 23-of-33 passes for 362 yards and 3 touchdowns. He also rushed for a score. Joseph set a school record with 302 yards passing in the first half, breaking the previous school record of 276 yards set by Jack Coan vs. Central Michigan on Sept. 7, 2019.

2. Joseph became the 14th Badger to pass for 300 yards in a game and is the first since Braedyn Locke threw for 359 yards vs. Purdue on Oct. 5, 2024. Joseph's 362 yards are the 7th most by a Badger QB in school history.

3. Joseph was UW's leading rusher on the afternoon, rushing 9 times for 46 yards and had his first rushing TD as a Badger. His 408 total yards of offense are tied for the third-most in school history with UW legend Melvin Gordon inducted into the UW Hall of Fame this weekend.

4. WR Tyrell Henry set the school record for single-game catches with 14 receptions for 160 yards and a touchdown. Henry broke Matt Nyquist's previous school record of 13 catches vs. Iowa on Nov. 18, 1995.

5. Henry's 160 yards were a career high as he was the first Badger to have 150+ yards receiving in a game since Alex Erickson had 160 yards receiving against Minnesota on Nov. 29 2014. Henry became the first Badger to surpass 100 receiving yards in a game since Lance Mason posted 102 receiving yards against Middle Tennessee State on Sept. 6, 2025.

6. RB Darrion Dupree rushed 8 times for 29 yards and a touchdown.

7. WR Chris Brooks Jr. had 3 catches for a career-high 91 yards, including a 75-yard TD in the 2nd quarter. The 75-yard reception was the longest of Brooks Jr.'s career. Brooks Jr. is the first Badger to catch TDs in back-to-back games since WR Jayden Ballard caught TDs against MTSU and Alabama during non-conference play last year.

8. TE Jacob Harris had 3 catches for 89 yards, matching his career high in receptions while setting a career-high in yards.

9. TE Emmett Bork had his first career reception, a 7-yard TD catch, in the fourth quarter.

10. CB Bryce West collected a career-high 5 tackles, which also led the team. His 2 tackles-for-loss were also a career best.

11. DL Nolan Vils had a career day with 5 tackles. He also posted his first career sack.

12. LB Sebastian Cheeks had a sack and forced fumble, his second forced fumble of the season. His forced fumble led to a scoop and score touchdown by Cooper Catalano.

13. LB Cooper Catalano had 4 tackles and his first career touchdown, recovering a fumble in the third quarter and running it in 10 yards for a score.

14. LB Mason Posa had his first career interception in the second quarter, running it back 24 yards. He also posted 3 stops.

15. S Matt Jung had his first pick as a Badger in the second quarter. In addition, he had 3 tackles, a pass breakup and a QB hurry.

16. K Gavin Lahm hit field goals from 39 yards and 41 yards and was a perfect 6-for-6 on extra points.

articles.title: Does Indiana's defense have problems after second straight shutout? Overreactions from win vs WKU
articles.summary: It's time to overreact: How many Hoosiers are Heisman contenders? Nick Marsh had his best game, and is the defense ready for Big Ten play? What we learned.
articles.body:
BLOOMINGTON — Indiana started sluggishly but accelerated away from Western Kentucky in a 38-0 win Saturday, finishing the No. 4 Hoosiers ' nonconference slate.

Classifying this as an overreaction probably depends on your particular concern.

It's two games in three now that the Hoosiers haven't looked quite so dominant as we expected at the line of scrimmage. Indiana's secondary still looks like a work in progress, which, considering injuries and the lived experience of some early season busts last year, is perhaps not hugely surprising.

Perhaps most notably, IU isn't forcing turnovers at nearly the rate it did a season ago. The Hoosiers gained 30 takeaways in 64 quarters last year, but have just three through 12 so far this fall.

You can find some concern in all that and still recognize that this is a unit that's allowed 16 points through three games. It shouldn't look like a finished product in September. But it can get better, and probably will.

This isn't an overreaction purely because the last guy won it, and the one before was a fringe candidate as well. Still, we won't preemptively anoint anyone as New York-bound.

Josh Hoover (649 yards, 10 touchdowns, zero interceptions) has looked very good through his first three games as a Hoosier. Even allowing for the competition, he's looked calm, poised and comfortable, and made some high-difficulty throws. His connections with Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh continue to expand, and the offense continues to build around Hoover himself.

Cignetti will have points of criticism. Not least a pair of missed throws to Marsh — one on a fourth-down slant route and the other a sideline vertical — that might have been touchdowns Saturday, if they'd been on target. Like Fernando Mendoza before him, Hoover still has room to grow in this offense. If he does, the same attention Mendoza got will find its way back to Bloomington.

Don't laugh at this one. If Jeremiah Smith is on the shortlist, Becker should be too.

He's got six touchdowns through three games. His highlight reel expands by the week. We know what he's capable of, even against better competition than this.

It's obviously very difficult for a receiver to get Heisman traction. We're not suggesting Becker will win it. But if we're going to include a player like Smith in those conversations, Becker probably deserves a place as well.

This isn't an overreaction at all. He was sharp, explosive and dangerous.

Cignetti will harp on his fumble, which Marsh was admittedly fortunate to recover. But after two weeks of Hoover-to-Becker dominating the passing game, it should be broadly encouraging to see Marsh step into a leading role this week. Becker led all Hoosiers with 127 yards receiving, but Marsh's 10 targets were tops on the team, and he finished with seven catches for 81 yards. His downfield blocking remains outstanding as well.

The more that turns into a two-man receiving attack, the more dangerous this offense becomes.

This is hardly an overreaction. This team has room to grow, but it's also clearly one of the best teams in the conference once again.

Perhaps it would be more accurate to say this team needs Big Ten play. It's learned all it can from these largely forgettable nonconference games . Indiana goes forward or not based on what it does against someone its own size from here going forward.

The Hoosiers are ready for league play, but more specifically, the season is ready for league play. This team needs those tests, and we'll learn a lot more once they arrive.

articles.title: Mets owner Steve Cohen talks team's future, front office discussions, Pete Alonso's return to Citi Field
articles.summary: On the day of Carlos Beltran’s number retirement ceremony at Citi Field, a special and joyous occasion for the club and all those involved, Mets owner Steve...
articles.body:
On the day of Carlos Beltran 's number retirement ceremony at Citi Field, a special and joyous occasion for the club and all those involved, Mets owner Steve Cohen made sure to also address the elephant in the room – what's been bubbling up for many Met fans this season, particularly this past week.

Speaking with the SNY booth in the fourth inning on Saturday, Cohen was asked about the recent shenanigans that happened at the ballpark during the team's last series with the Baltimore Orioles .

In what was Pete Alonso 's first time back in Queens since he left the Mets in free agency over the offseason, fans came out in droves and gave the first baseman quite the reception. Not only did they give Alonso a standing ovation in his first at-bat, standard for a former beloved player coming back to his old ballpark, fans were actively cheering for Alonso's success every time he went to the plate.

Things got murky when Alonso, who was chasing his 300th career home run, hit the milestone by hitting a game-tying home run against Kodai Senga in the top of the ninth inning which caused the stadium to erupt in cheers – odd for a home ballpark.

The Mets went on to lose that game in extra innings and during the postgame, players, including Sean Manaea and Francisco Lindor , admitted to being surprised by the response of the home fans seemingly cheering against their team.

"You can't make it up, it was just so crazy," Cohen said on Saturday. "The fans, they're passionate and when they feel something they're gonna let you know and I'm okay with that. Pete hits his 300th home run and it was sort of poetic. It was sort of amazing that it all occurred at the same time."

Cohen seemed to understand where the fans were coming from, letting their frustration out for a player they believed deserved to be a lifetime Met.

Of course, that's not how things turned out and in the midst of a disappointing season, it made it all the more painful.

"I'll say it again, it didn't surprise me," Cohen said about the fan's response to Alonso's return. "I can remember being at a previous Mets event the previous year and the fans were vocal on Alonso and listen, it's hard to say goodbye to a home grown player. Obviously he's well liked and a great Met and those decisions got made and unfortunately we gotta look forward and look forward to '27 and what we're gonna do.

"But it was weird because we got past the trade deadline and the team was playing well and you got a sense that fans were really getting excited and then Pete came in and we kinda reversed course for three days, but now I think we're back on track again."

It's true, prior to Alonso's homecoming, despite the lost season, fans seemed to be invested in the team because of the young talent that spurred hope for the future, as well as the team's improved performance on the field, albeit too late.

Still, Cohen believed that what the Mets had been building was enough to garner enthusiasm for what's to come, even if it came during a second consecutive season missing the playoffs.

"I think that's what the fans like," he said. "We're playing young, we're playing athletic. We've developed a lot of players in a very short period of time and so that's something you can really look forward to. So it's true, two things can be true: a lousy season, but still something to look forward to."

Something else Mets fans can look forward to is help coming on the way for president of baseball operations David Stearns – both in terms of the front office as well as a manager.

Despite interim manager Andy Green' s success during his time leading the team, Cohen confirmed the team will be looking elsewhere for somebody to lead the team and spoke about what he wants to see out of his next manager, a conversation that fittingly happened during Beltran's number retirement ceremony.

"I see the manager's role as mostly about culture and bringing the locker room together," the owner said. 'I think the actual managerial decisions are, I would say, 20-30 percent of what they do and the rest of it is trying to galvanize your ball club and trying to get them in the right frame of mind and I'm looking for someone that can bring out the best in their ball players."

As for the front office, Cohen mentioned that he's "identified some things that we can do better" and talked about bringing in extra voices to the mix to help out.

"We're going to try to add certain voices into the front office that I think will be helpful and I know David supports that and I'm looking forward to, when we make those decisions, to announce them," he said.

Cohen continued: "It doesn't have to be a GM, it could be other ways to support David and the front office and I think the whole point is to get more opinions in the front office and people who are either pretty good at evaluating talent or people who have been in those positions before in the front office – in high positions – and help David out and help the team out as far as getting a different point of view."

Cohen was also asked how he deals with, as he described it, such passionate fans that are always eager to give their two cents in how to run the team.

"Everyone's got an opinion, I'll tell you that," he said. "…And frankly, there's some good ideas out there so my ears are open."

articles.title: Brexton Busch Joins Ty Gibbs for Emotional Bristol Introduction in Kyle Busch Tribute
articles.summary: Brexton Busch joined Ty Gibbs onstage during driver introductions at Bristol, sharing an emotional moment before Gibbs raced a special M&M's scheme honoring...
articles.body:
For one of the biggest introductions of the night at Bristol Motor Speedway, Ty Gibbs didn't walk onto the stage alone.

Gibbs received a loud reception from the Bristol crowd ahead of Saturday night's NASCAR Cup Series race , but the volume climbed another level when Brexton joined him onstage during driver introductions. The 11-year-old took the microphone as the two appeared together in front of the crowd.

It was already going to be an emotional night for the Busch family.

Gibbs is driving a special M&M's scheme honoring the late Kyle Busch, bringing one of the most recognizable paint schemes of Busch's career back onto a Cup Series car. At Bristol, a track so closely tied to Busch's career and legacy, seeing Brexton alongside the driver entrusted with that tribute made the moment hit differently.

It also wasn't a ceremonial pairing manufactured for Saturday night.

In the months since Kyle's death, Gibbs has become a mentor and friend to Brexton as the young racer continues pursuing his own career. That relationship was on full display at Bristol before either Gibbs or his tribute car ever took the green flag.

Ty Gibbs and Brexton Busch share Bristol spotlight

Brexton accompanied Gibbs during the pre-race festivities before eventually joining him onstage for driver introductions.

Gibbs drew big cheers when he was introduced. Brexton's appearance brought an even louder response from the Bristol crowd as he stepped onto the stage and took the microphone.

For Gibbs, the moment added another layer to a weekend that was already about far more than one race result.

The Joe Gibbs Racing driver is carrying the familiar M&M's colors once synonymous with Busch, putting the scheme back on track as part of Bristol's tribute to the two-time Cup Series champion. Gibbs' connection to Busch makes him a fitting driver for the honor, but his growing relationship with Brexton has made the tribute considerably more personal.

Brexton has continued racing since losing his father, navigating a season no young driver could have prepared for. Gibbs has emerged as one of the NASCAR figures helping him through it, offering the kind of guidance that extends beyond what happens behind the wheel.

Saturday offered a public glimpse of that bond.

Rather than simply watching the tribute to his father unfold from the sidelines, Brexton became part of it.

Kyle Busch's Bristol legacy adds another layer to the tribute

There could hardly be a more fitting place for the moment.

Bristol was one of the defining tracks of Kyle Busch's NASCAR career. He won eight Cup Series races at the Tennessee short track, and his relationship with the Bristol crowd became part of the show itself.

Busch could make the grandstands erupt in cheers or boos, sometimes seemingly in equal measure. Either way, Bristol reacted to him.

That history has made his absence particularly noticeable this weekend.

But Saturday's pre-race scene also showed how Busch's influence continues through the people he left behind. His colors are back on the racetrack. His son is continuing to pursue racing. And one of the Cup Series drivers helping Brexton navigate that path is now carrying a paint scheme synonymous with his father's career.

There was no need to manufacture the symbolism.

Brexton standing beside Gibbs said enough.

Once driver introductions ended, Gibbs still had a race to run and an M&M's tribute car to bring onto one of NASCAR's most unforgiving tracks .

But before any of that happened, Bristol gave Brexton Busch one of the night's biggest welcomes.

And he got to experience it alongside someone who has become an important part of his racing journey.

articles.title: Music City Miscue gives Vanderbilt a win over NC State no one saw coming
articles.summary: Call this one the Music City Miscue.  N.C. State quarterback CJ Bailey fumbled in the end zone while trying to run out the clock or potentially take a safety...
articles.body:
N.C. State quarterback CJ Bailey fumbled in the end zone while trying to run out the clock or potentially take a safety in the final seconds and then handed Vanderbilt a 35-31 victory no one saw coming in Nashville.

It was as improbable a finish as the Music City Miracle , the famous last-second kickoff return in January 2000 that gave the NFL's Tennessee Titans a 22–16 playoff win over the Buffalo Bills .

"I can't put into words what I felt. ... You get one of those in a lifetime," Vanderbilt coach Clark Lea said. "We cheated the football gods today and got away with it."

Bailey and the Wolfpack (1-2) were attempting to milk the clock on the final snap, a fourth-and-3 play from their 5-yard line with six seconds remaining.

Miles Capers knocked the ball out of Bailey's hands, and Cayden Van Daniels recovered it in the end zone for a touchdown. It capped Vanderbilt's rally from a 17-0 deficit in the first half.

"It's having true brotherhood," Capers said. "We trust each other, we're going to play for each other, and we know that we not out of the fight no matter what."

The ending was reminiscent of Miami's debacle against Georgia Tech in October 2023, when Hurricanes coach Mario Cristobal chose to run the ball instead of taking a knee with 26 seconds left and no timeouts remaining for Georgia Tech. Miami 's Donald Chaney Jr. fumbled, Georgia Tech's Kyle Canard recovered and the Yellow Jackets won on a 44-yard touchdown pass from Haynes King to Christian Leary.

N.C. State coach Dave Doeren surely will lament his decision. The Wolfpack could have simply punted and played defense for a play or had Bailey run out of the back of the end zone for a surefire safety.

N.C. State was looking for its first road win against a Southeastern Conference opponent since 1977. Vanderbilt (3-0) matched its largest comeback victory since beating Ole Miss in 2012. Vandy's fumble recovery in the end zone ended up being the team's only lead of the game.

According to ESPN, college football teams were 1,046-1 over the last 20 seasons when having the ball and the lead with 10 seconds to go in a game. The lone loss: Michigan falling to rival Michigan State in 2015.

articles.title: Mookie Betts Could Take Shohei Ohtani’s Leadoff Spot When Dodgers Star Returns
articles.summary: Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts addressed the team's lead-off position as Shohei Ohtani sits and Mookie Betts thrives.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts addressed the team's lead-off position as Shohei Ohtani sits and Mookie Betts thrives.

On Saturday, September 19th, Roberts was asked directly whether Ohtani would lead off when he returned from the injured list, Dodgers Nation's Noel Sanchez reports.

"I mean, I think that's my first kind of thought," Roberts said to the media, including Dodgers Nation.

"But until he gets back, or when he gets back, then I'll kind of potentially read and react if it's a left-right situation. I haven't really thought too much about it."

Ohtani is on the IL with right arm/bicep soreness, which surfaced during his pitching work. He's also battling left knee soreness.

The Dodgers hope rest will help Ohtani, who looked like a shell of his best self in his last few at-bats before sitting out.

Over the last few days, Ohtani has been doing light baseball work and is trending in a good direction, according to Dave Roberts, leaving the door open for him to get some plate appearances before the postseason.

As the Dodgers found out, a compromised Ohtani cannot touch the same heights as a fully healthy one. As the injuries racked up and the wear led to a hampered swing, Ohtani was not delivering at a level to merit the lead-off spot.

Ohtani hit just .186/.324/.390 in his last 15 games, with production looking really bad over the last seven games: .077 with a .250 OBP.

While Ohtani has dropped off, Mookie Betts has started heating up and is now taking over the leadoff spot in Ohtani's absence.

For most of Ohtani's time out injured, which has been a few weeks now, Tommy Edman has handled most of the lead-off work.

However, Edman is now hitting .135/.274/.231 at lead-off, and Betts is really getting going.

Betts is hitting .356 with a .457 OBP over his last 15 games. Over 30 games, Betts is hitting .298/.384/.529.

Roberts talked about deploying Betts at leadoff for a second straight game, even against a righty pitcher

"I think that certainly there is uncertainty with Shohei, all the while expecting to be back. But you do have to prepare for whatever," Roberts said to the media, including Dodgers Nation.

"I just think Mookie swinging the bat well and has many times throughout his career. It just kind of makes sense."

If Betts keeps this up and Ohtani returns still limited, Roberts will have to think hard about moving the batting order to improve the team's three-peat odds.

articles.title: Saturday Seacoast Roundup: PCA volleyball sweeps tri-match, more results
articles.summary: The Portsmouth Christian Academy volleyball team swept a Division III tri-match. Check out all the reported scores from across the Seacoast on Saturday.
articles.body:
DOVER — The Portsmouth Christian Academy volleyball team extended its unbeaten start to the season by sweeping a Division III tri-match Saturday, defeating Inter-Lakes and Sunapee.

The Eagles opened the day with a 3-1 victory over Inter-Lakes by scores of 25-15, 19-25, 25-18 and 25-21. Dylan Anderson led the offense with 14 kills, 11 digs and two blocks, while Molly Marquis added 10 kills, six aces and 13 digs. Bea Monahan recorded 24 assists, three aces and 13 digs, and Caroline Braman chipped in seven kills, two aces and seven digs.

PCA then completed the sweep with a 3-0 win over Sunapee, taking the sets 25-14, 25-8 and 25-13. Marquis paced the Eagles with five kills, seven aces and six digs. Monahan contributed 17 assists, six aces and five digs, while Dylan Anderson and Sawyer Yim each had five kills. Yim also added four aces and six digs, and Braman finished with four kills, two aces and two blocks.

The Eagles improved to 6-0 and will host Hillsboro-Deering on Wednesday.

WEARE — Paige Demers led Somersworth with nine kills and reached a milestone in the victory, recording her 219th career block to set a school record.

Individual set scores were 25-15, 25-17 and 25-10.

Emily Runions and Abby Brown both had six kills for Somersworth (6-0), while Kylie Pettengill had 22 assists, and Gishella Lumingkewas had 17 service points.

The win improved Somersworth to 5-0 on the season.

EPPING - Gavin McKenna and Sawyer Rabb each scored a goal for Newmarket in its Division IV contest.

SOMERSWORTH - The Hilltoppers, who were led by Tyler Runions, fell to 2-5 on the season after this Division IV loss.

CAPE ELIZABETH, Maine — Drew Trenholm scored York's one goal in this Class B South loss. Cape Elizabeth on Saturday.

Chris Adams and Max Hayward each scored a goal for Cape Elizabeth.
